problems.title: [Inorganic analogues of carbon compounds]
problems.problem:
Problem 6 (Inorganic Chemistry section, problem 3). [Inorganic analogues of carbon compounds]

Carbon is like gold: it is shiny and precious. (Russian national proverb)

In inorganic chemistry there are substances with physical and chemical properties similar to organic. In this problem, you are invited to meet with three groups of compounds are examples of such similarities.

Carbon has a large number of allotropic modifications – graphite, diamond, fullerenes, graphene, carbon nanotubes. Inorganic binary compound $\mathbf{E}$ can form a structure similar to all of the above. $(\mathbf{E})_3$ is isoelectronic to $\ce{C6}$ cell in the graphite structure. The ratio of elements of the $\mathbf{E}$ is 1: 1. At a pressure of 7 GPa and a temperature of $1500\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ $\mathbf{E}$ becomes crystal structure of diamond. The hardness of $\mathbf{E}$ is less than diamond, but more durable, heat-resistant and chemically resistant, so it is widely used for polishing steel.

The elements included in the $\mathbf{E}$, also form $\mathbf{M}$ – a colorless liquid, which is also called "inorganic benzene" for a similar smell, and a ring structure with a system of delocalized π-electrons. Due to the difference in the electronegativities of the atoms included in the $\mathbf{M}$, it is more reactive in addition reactions compared to benzene.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2016-2-6-fig1.png

1. Determine the $\mathbf{M}$ and $\mathbf{E}$, write the reaction equations represented in the scheme.

2. Write a reaction that may occur in the processing of steel diamond polish wheels and reduce their service.

In addition to the $\mathbf{E}$ some transition metals compounds have structures similar to allotropic carbon modifications too. The most active work is carried out to obtain "inorganic graphene" based on them for the creation of optoelectronic semiconductors. Binary substance $\mathbf{N}$ was one of the first, which managed to obtain monolayers with a similar layer structure of graphene. Obtaining a given structure of $\mathbf{N}$ occurs in several stages. At first, thermal decomposition of $10^{-3}$ mol of ammonium salt $\mathbf{B}$ produces 178 mL of gas with a sharp odor at $90\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and a pressure of 1 atm, 1.008 g of the oxide $\mathbf{O}$ of hexavalent metal $\mathbf{C}$ (the oxygen content of the oxide $\mathbf{O}$ is 33.3% mass) and 89 mL water vapor. Further, monolayers $\mathbf{N}$ are formed after the interaction between $\mathbf{O}$ and hydrogen sulfide in a stream of hydrogen at $400\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

3. Determine the $\mathbf{N}$, $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{C}$. What side product will be formed if the reaction is carried out without hydrogen? Write the equation of this reaction.

After 20 days after the closing ceremony of the 49th International Mendeleev Olympiad an article was published in Science Journal by scientist from MIT about how to obtain inorganic ion $\mathrm{P}_x\mathrm{N}_y^-$ – analogue of cyclopentadienyl anion (Cp). According to the mass spectrum of $\mathrm{P}_x\mathrm{N}_y^-$, his mass number m/z = 104 was defined.

4. a) determine the molecular formula of the anion, if it is known that two signals are observed in the spectrum of $^{15}$N NMR, $x$ and $y$ are integers number;

b) draw resonance structures of $\mathrm{P}_x\mathrm{N}_y^-$.

In addition to $\mathrm{P}_x\mathrm{N}_y^-$ there are other inorganic compounds containing phosphorus, nitrogen and sulfur and being isoelectronic to Cp;

c) write three molecular formula of the respective cation, anion and molecule.

5. a) write a Hückel rule for aromaticity for organic substances;

b) determine the number of $\pi$-electrons in $\mathbf{M}$ and $\mathrm{P}_x\mathrm{N}_y^-$.

problems.title: [Ortho- and para-hydrogen]
problems.problem:
Problem 7 (Physical Chemistry section, problem 1). [Ortho- and para-hydrogen]

The molecules $\mathbf{A}_2$, formed by nuclides with $i \neq 0$, have nucleus isomers. The nuclei of atoms $\mathbf{A}$ with odd number of nucleons are described by Fermi – Dirac statistics and ortho-isomer ($o$-$\mathbf{A}_2$) has odd total spin $I$ ($I = \Sigma i$), para-isomer ($p$-$\mathbf{A}_2$) – even.

1. Give $I$ for $o$-$\ce{H2}$ and $p$-$\ce{H2}$. Indicate the orientation of spins by arrows.

For the reaction $p$-$\ce{H2} \rightleftarrows o$-$\ce{H2}$ the equilibrium constant $K = \chi_\mathrm{o}/\chi_\mathrm{p} = f(T)$ at low $T$ (see table), and at high – $K \neq f(T)$. $K$ = 2.98 (400 K); 3.00 (500 K); 3.00 (600 K).

2. Derivate the equation $\ln K = A + B/T$ if $\Delta G^0 = -RT\ln K$ and $\Delta G^0 = \Delta H^0 - T\Delta S^0$. Using $\chi_i$, calculate $A_\mathrm{av}$ and $B_\mathrm{av}$ and fill the gaps in the table.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c} T,\ \mathrm{K} & 20 & 30 & 40 & 60 & 100 \\ \hline \chi_\mathrm{p},\ \text{mol.\%} & & 97.0 & & 65.8 & 38.6 \\ \hline K & 1.89\cdot10^{-3} & & 0.127 & & \end{array}$$

3. Calculate $\Delta H^0$ and $\Delta S^0$, considering, that they are independent of $T$.

In 2010 J. Ingues proposed three step scheme for the reaction at high $T$. At the first step $p$-$\ce{H2}$ (1 atm, 600 K, $V$, $\chi_\mathrm{p} = 1$) transforms to $o$-$\ce{H2}$ (1 atm, 600 K, $V$, $\chi_\mathrm{o} = x$) and $p$-$\ce{H2}$ (1 atm, 600 K, $V$, $\chi_\mathrm{p} = 1 - x$) with entropy $\Delta S_\mathrm{I} = 9.2x\,\mathrm{J/K}$. At the second step $o$-$\ce{H2}$ and $p$-$\ce{H2}$ mix together and entropy equals $\Delta S_\mathrm{II} = -R[x\ln x + (1-x)\ln(1-x)]$. At the third step – $T$ changes and $\Delta S_\mathrm{III} = C_V\cdot\ln(T/600)$.

4. Give the condition, at which $K \neq f(T)$ if $d\ln K/dT = \Delta H^\circ/RT^2$.

5. Calculate $\Delta S_\mathrm{I+II} = \Delta S_\mathrm{I} + \Delta S_\mathrm{II}$ for $x$ = 0.6, 0.7, 0.8 and 0.85. Build the graph $\Delta S_\mathrm{I+II} = f(x)$, determine $x$ for $\Delta S_\mathrm{I+II}$ = max, calculate for it $K_0$ and compare with given in the condition $K$ for high $T$.

6. Determine the minimal $T$, at which the scheme works, if entropy change in the reaction and at change of $T$ are equal and $C_V = 20.9\,\mathrm{J/mol\cdot K}$.

The nuclei of atoms $\mathbf{A}$ with even number of nucleons are described by Bose – Einstein statistics and $o$-$\mathbf{A}_2$ has even spin, and $p$-$\mathbf{A}_2$ – odd. The value $\chi_i$ is proportional to the possible conditions $2I + 1$.

7. Give $I$ for ortho- and para-isomers of deuterium ($o$-$\ce{D2}$ and $p$-$\ce{D2}$).

8. Calculate the maximal possible content of isomers for $\ce{H2}$ and $\ce{D2}$ and show the stable ones.

The Born – Haber cycle based on Hess law, is a convenient graphical method for studying the thermodynamics of chemical reactions. Such a cycle for the formation reaction of the chloride of metal $\mathbf{A}$, which comparing two ways of this process – from simple substances (I) and an ideal gas of ions of the substance (VII), is shown in left figure. The latter passes through the stages: sublimation of $\mathbf{A}$ (II), ionization of $\mathbf{A}$ (III, IV), dissociation of chlorine (V), ionization of chlorine atoms (VI).

Upon dissolution of the carbonate of metal $\mathbf{A}$ in the hydrochloric acid 69.7 kJ of heat is absorbed $\mathbf{A}\mathrm{CO_3(s)} + \mathrm{2HCl(l)} = \mathbf{A}\mathrm{Cl_2(sol)} + \mathrm{CO_2(g)} + \mathrm{H_2O(l)}$. $\mathbf{A}\mathrm{Cl_2}$ crystallizes from the solution as hexahydrate. For it's decomposition with the aim of obtaining anhydrous salt it is necessary to spend 344.3 kJ of heat.

The above cycle describes the processes that occur at a fixed temperature, pressure and other parameters. Building of three-dimensional Born – Haber cycle with changeable external parameters allows to predict the most thermodynamically favored route of complex chemical reactions. In the following figure, as an example, a diagram of a simple reaction between metal $\mathbf{A}$ and hydrochloric acid at three different temperatures of 348, 298 and 170 K (the scale of energy is not respected) is shown. Problem 9 (Physical Chemistry section, problem 3). [Kinetic scheme of a heterogeneous catalytic reaction]

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2016-2-9-fig1.png

In the physical chemistry no way exist for prediction of activity of catalyst in certain reaction based on its physico-chemical properties meaning that there is no "general theory of catalysis". For the prediction understanding of mechanism of catalytic reaction is required. To determine the mechanism one often carry out kinetic investigation of the reaction and establish the kinetic scheme approximately. The scheme consist of sequence of intermediate compounds and by-products obtaining in the course of reaction.

A schematic diagram of reactor used in heterogeneous catalytic reactions, widespread in the industry, is illustrated in the Figure. For quantitative determination of activity of catalyst conversion $C$ of the raw (mole fraction of reacted raw with respect to raw fed), selectivity $S(X)$ on target product $\mathbf{X}$ (mole fraction of $\mathbf{X}$ with respect to all products) and yield $Y(X)$ of product $\mathbf{X}$ are in common use.

1. Derive the equation for yield on product $\mathbf{X}$ using conversion of raw and selectivity on product $\mathbf{X}$.

For the investigation of kinetic scheme one vary contact time of catalyst with raw. Since it is easier to change WHSV (weight hourly space velocity, or feed rate) without changes in catalyst weight, one does it by this way. After that one analyze distribution of products depending on feed rate and suppose kinetic scheme of reaction.

2. Derive the equation for contact time ($\tau$, s) of catalyst with raw using catalyst weight ($m$, kg), its bulk density ($\rho$, $\mathrm{kg/m^3}$) and raw feed rate ($V$, L/min).

Investigation of catalytic conversion of A into B was carried out in continous flow reactor at $200\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The catalyst weight was 0.5 kg in all experiments and its bulk density was $1000\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$. Feed rate was changed in the range of 1 – 30 L/min. It was discovered that by-products $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{D}$ and $\mathbf{E}$ are obtained beside $\mathbf{B}$ and unreacted $\mathbf{A}$. For each feed rate yield of $\mathbf{A}$ – $\mathbf{E}$ products was calculated and given in the Table.

4. a) Calculate conversion of $\mathbf{A}$ for all feed rate values (fill the Table in the answer sheet); b) Which function describes the dependence of conversion of $\mathbf{A}$ on contact time if only irreversible $\mathbf{A}$ to $\mathbf{B}$ transformation occurs over the catalyst?

problems.problem:
Problem 10 (Life Sciences and Polymers section, problem 1). [Interpolyelectrolyte complexes of chitosan]

Macromolecules of polyelectrolytes (PE) contain groups capable of dissociation in aqueous solutions. PEs can interact with other charged species via the ion exchange mechanism.

1. Draw structures of the repeating units of the polymers listed in the Answer Sheet. Of these, select a pair of PEs that react with one another in their aqueous solution to form an interpolyelectrolyte complex.

A water-soluble polymer chitosan is prepared via hydrolysis of natural polymer chitin (see the structure in the Answer Sheet) in the presence of acetic acid.

[The list of polymers for question 1 and the structure of chitin are printed only in the Answer Sheet, which is not available.]

2. Draw a scheme of chitin hydrolysis yielding chitosan and determine the amount of charged groups per one chitosan macromolecule if its molecular mass is 492310 g/mol and the average molecular mass of the repeating unit is 164.10 g/mol.

Chitosan exists in the form of polycation in acidic aqueous solutions, thus being capable of interacting with negatively charged species. For example, the interaction of aqueous solutions of chitosan and compound $\mathbf{A}$ (50.00 wt.% C, 5.60 wt.% H, 44.40 wt.% O) gives a loose precipitate of the interpolyelectrolyte complex. The freezing point of 1 wt% aqueous solution of sodium salt of $\mathbf{A}$ (the cryoscopic constant of water is of $1.86\,\mathrm{kg\cdot deg/mol}$) equals $-0.208\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

3. Determine the gross formula and molecular mass of $\mathbf{A}$. Take that dissociation of $\mathbf{A}$ is complete.

Yellow substance $\mathbf{B}$ prepared by interaction of ammonium molybdate(VI) with phosphoric acid in an excess of nitric acid (not a redox reaction) belongs to a special class of compounds containing a polyvalent anion of complex structure. The corresponding acids behave similar to polyacids and are capable of the interacting with polybases to form interpolyelectrolyte complexes.

4. a) Write down the equation of formation of $\mathbf{B}$. Note that drying of $\mathbf{B}$ to constant mass at $150\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ leads to the residue with the metal content of 61.36% and phosphorus content of 1.65%.

b) How many anions of $\mathbf{B}$ per the chitosan molecule (see i. 2) are found in the stoichiometric polycomplex? If you have failed to give the answer in i. 2, take $N$ as the number of ionogenic groups in the chitosan molecule.

Enthalpy of the reactions of polyelectrolyte complex formation being close to zero, these reactions occur owing to high positive entropy change, which is due to the release of small ions initially located in the vicinity of the polyion into the bulk solution.

5. Indicate the low-molecular weight ions released in the course of interaction of:

a) the polyelectrolytes chosen in i. 1

b) chitosan and the acid corresponding to $\mathbf{B}$. If you have failed to give the answer in i. 1, 2, or 4, give your own examples of the interacting polyelectrolytes (no more than two pairs), drawing their structures in the Answers Sheet.

The entropy increase owing to the small ions release into the bulk solution is partially compensated by an unfavorable change of entropy due to binding of the polyions (these polymers initially distributed in the entire volume of the reaction mixture are later found in the precipitate of the insoluble complex). Note that entropy is related to the number of microscopic states of the system which provide for its macroscopic state.

6. Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their tendency towards complex formation with chitosan: tribromoacetic acid $\mathbf{C}$, acid $\mathbf{A}$, and the acid corresponding to $\mathbf{B}$. Determine the element with the highest content (by mass) in the dried precipitate of the chitosan complex with a mixture of these acids (each of three acids taken in an excess with respect to the stoichiometric ratio).

problems.title: [Sous-vide cooking]
problems.problem:
Problem 11 (Life Sciences and Polymers section, problem 2). [Sous-vide cooking]

To the authors of task 6 at IChO-2015, big connoisseurs of freshly baked bread

Cooking in vacuum (fr. sous-vide) is a method when meat or vegetables are placed into a sealed airtight plastic bag and simmered long at relatively low and controlled temperature, usually in a water-bath. The method is characterized by a number of advantages. In the case of meat slabs (usually boiled or braised) the correct choice of temperature (~$60\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) provides for complete transformation of muscular collagen (fibrillar protein, the major component of connective tissue) into gelatin with maximum retention of the meat succulence.

1. Write down (in general form) the reaction equation of collagen transformation into gelatin.

The color of beef is by 90-95% due to the protein of myoglobin, specifically to the ratio of its three forms differing in the corresponding ion and/or the ligand bound:

• Myoglobin (Mb), containing $\ce{Fe^{2+}}$ and water molecule;
• Oxymyoglobin ($\mathrm{MbO_2}$), containing $\ce{Fe^{2+}}$ and oxygen molecule;
• Metmyoglobin (MMb+), containing $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$ and water molecule.

Fresh-killed meat is of deeper color inside the slab as compared to its external parts, and is practically free of MMb+. Due to precise temperature control and uniform heating of the slab, Sous-vide allows cooking ideal steaks with different degree of doneness accordingly differing in the meat color.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \textbf{The degree of steak doneness} & \textbf{Color} & \textbf{Temperature of cooking, }{}^\circ\mathbf{C} \\ \hline \text{Extra-rare or Blue (bleu)} & \text{Rich red} & 46\text{–}49 \\ \hline \text{Medium (demi-anglais)} & \text{Pink in the center, more read towards the outer parts} & 60\text{–}65 \\ \hline \text{Well done (bien cuit)} & \text{Grey-brown} & 71 \\ \hline \text{Overcooked (trop cuit)} & \text{Black} & >100 \end{array}$$

2. Determine the prevailing myoglobin form (Mb, $\mathrm{MbO_2}$ or MMb+) at each of the mentioned above degrees of steak doneness.

3. What other process developing in the course of sous-vide cooking of meat can be behind the taste difference depending on the degree of steak doneness.

Conventional meat panbroiling leads to typical dish smell, color and taste. This is mostly due to the formation of Maillard reaction products (occurs at t > $150\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$). Impossibility of Maillard reaction is one of sous-vide drawbacks disappointing gourmands.

Compound $\mathbf{X}$ providing a dish with the smell of butter is formed via Maillard reaction. The formula of $\mathbf{X}$ can be represented as $\mathrm{C}_p\mathrm{H}_q\mathrm{O}_r$. It obeys two following equations: $p + q + r = 12$ (1) and $p\cdot q\cdot r = 48$ (2).

4. Derive the molecular formula of $\mathbf{X}$ if the mass content of hydrogen in $\mathbf{X}$ exceeds 7%.

5. Draw the structural formula of $\mathbf{X}$ if it is known that $\mathbf{X}$ contains 2 types of C atoms and one type of H and O atoms each.

On the other hand, sous-vide allows avoiding a number of toxic products, such as $\mathbf{Y}$ ($\ce{C3H5NO}$). $\mathbf{Y}$ is formed by Maillard reaction from amino acid asparagine and a 1,2-dicarbonyl compound (e.g., 3-deoxyglucosone, a D-glucose derivative) according to the hereunder scheme (reaction equations at all stages):

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2016-2-11-fig1.png

It is known that $\mathbf{G}$ and $\mathbf{L}$ are binary substances.

6. Draw the 3-deoxyglucosone structure in Fischer projection.

7. Draw the structural formulae of $\mathbf{A}$ – $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{G}$, $\mathbf{L}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$.

Compound $\mathbf{Z}$ is an $\mathbf{Y}$ metabolite. Being a mutagen $\mathbf{Z}$ is a hazardous substance for man. $\mathbf{X}$ transformation into $\mathbf{Z}$ is a single-stage enzymatically catalyzed process. $\mathbf{Z}$ contains 36.75% O and 41.38% C by mass and has an asymmetric C atom.

8. Write down the structural formula of $\mathbf{Z}$.

problems.title: [Poisons and antidotes]
problems.problem:
Problem 12 (Life Sciences and Polymers section, problem 3). [Poisons and antidotes]

All things are poison and nothing is without poison; only the dose makes a thing not a poison. Paracelsus

Toxicology deals with poisons and mechanisms of their action. Poisons are substances causing disruption of vital activity of an organism when present in it in relatively small doses (thus, as little as 100 ng of particular protein toxins and as much as 200 g of sodium chloride lead to fatal case in man). Since, a human being is in every day contact with various chemicals, knowledge of their toxicological properties as well as the first aid measures in the case of intoxication is vitally important. Substances easing the influence of poisons on organisms are referred to as antidotes.

1. Names of some substances ($\mathbf{1}$ – $\mathbf{5}$) often met in chemical labs are given in the hereunder table. Penetration of these substances into organisms leads to intoxication. Based on their chemical properties, correlate in the Answer Sheet each substance with the structure of its antidote ($\mathbf{A}$ – $\mathbf{E}$).

$$\begin{array}{c|l} \mathbf{1} & \text{white arsenic} \\ \hline \mathbf{2} & \text{methanol} \\ \hline \mathbf{3} & \text{hydrofluoric acid} \\ \hline \mathbf{4} & \text{lead sugar} \\ \hline \mathbf{5} & \text{carbon monooxide} \end{array}$$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2016-2-12-fig1.png

Cyanide is the favorite poison in detective novels, cytochrome c oxidase (an iron-containing enzyme of the respiratory chain) being its target in organisms. In the case of intoxication with potassium cyanide or vapors of hydrocyanic acid, it is needed to open an ampoule with isoamyl nitrite and let the sufferer inhale its vapors.

2. Draw the structure of isoamyl nitrite and write down the sequence of equations of three reactions occurring in blood, which explain the antidote action. Remember that hemoglobin is one of the blood components! Denote the unessential part of organic molecules as R.

After applying the first aid measures described above, sodium thioisulfate is administered to the patient intravenously.

3. Write down the equation of this final detoxication stage if two sulfur-containing particles are its low molecular weight products.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2016-2-12-fig2.png

Overdosing of drugs often leads to intoxication. Even well known preparations like $\mathbf{P}$ can be dangerous if overdosed. The toxicity of $\mathbf{P}$ is due to the product of its single stage enzymatic transformation $\mathbf{P1}$ (9.40% N by mass) with one of antidotes ($\mathbf{A}$ – $\mathbf{E}$) being a reagent in this transformation.

4. Deduce the structure of $\mathbf{P1}$ if the number of the carbon atoms is not changed in the transformation from $\mathbf{P}$.

$\mathbf{PA}$ ($\ce{C5H9NO3S}$) obtained by a single stage synthesis from a canonical amino acid acts as an antidote in the case of such intoxication. $\mathbf{PA}$ is a diprotic acid with $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}$ values of 3.2 and 11.2; its solutions decolorize $\ce{KI3}$ solution. $\mathbf{PA}$ enters into the reaction of nucleophilic addition to $\mathbf{P1}$, aromatic substance $\mathbf{P2}$ being the sole reaction product.

5. Deduce the structures of $\mathbf{PA}$ and $\mathbf{P2}$, write down the reaction schemes.

Overdosing of $\mathbf{P}$ leads to liver injury induced by $\mathbf{P1}$.

6. Exhaustion of what biologically important molecules is behind the liver injury? Choose the correct variant in the Answer Sheet.

[The variants for question 6 are printed only in the Answer Sheet, which is not available.]

$\mathbf{X1}$ is one of the most potent (still slow-response) poisons. This is a three-element metal salt. Penetration of as low as 1 ng of this substance into the organism can turn out to be lethal. The intoxication manifests in gradual development of sickness, head-ache, hyperthermia, blood effusion, gastrointestinal upset and mental breakdown. The numbers of atoms in the formula unit of $\mathbf{X1}$ are a geometrical progression, the total sum of the numbers does not exceed 15, and the mass content of carbon equals 16.2%.

7. Do calculations to determine $\mathbf{X1}$ and write down the reaction equation explaining its toxicity. Write down the reaction of thermal decomposition of $\mathbf{X1}$.

The Robinson annulation is very important reaction in the synthesis of various natural compounds, antibiotics, steroids, etc. This reaction consists of the following steps: ketone deprotonation, Michael addition of the formed enolate ion to methyl vinyl ketone (or its derivative), aldol condensation producing the corresponding cyclohexanone derivative.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2016-2-13-fig1.png

Two reactions are given below. Compound $\mathbf{X}$ is the product of the Robinson annulation. Oppositely, $\mathbf{Y}$ has no two annulated rings but has two different C=O groups despite its formation includes the Michael addition step.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2016-2-13-fig2.png

1. Write down structural formulae of $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$.

Compound $\mathbf{X}$ was used in the total synthesis of anticancer terpenoid (±)-widdrol:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2016-2-13-fig3.png

2. Write down structural formulae of $\mathbf{A}$ – $\mathbf{E}$.

3. Write down structural formulae of $\mathbf{F}$ – $\mathbf{M}$.

The efficient method for the synthesis of cyclic compounds is the cycloaddition reaction wherein two or more bonds are formed during a single reaction act. According to IUPAC recommendations, cycloaddition reactions can be classified by the number of participating atoms as (m+n+…)-cycloadditions.

2. Write down types of the cycloaddition reaction for the formation of $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$.

Use of transition metal complexes for catalysis of cycloadditions provides high efficiency of these processes. Mechanism for the formation of the compound $\mathbf{A}$ and its homologues in the presence of complex $\mathrm{ML_n}$ can be represented as:

Cycloadditions in the presence of transition metal complexes allow: a) to synthesize polycyclic structures from acyclic starting compounds; b) to prepare a ring simultaneously with the introduction of a functional group:

problems.title: [The lychee amino acid X]
problems.problem:
Problem 15 (Organic Chemistry section, problem 3). [The lychee amino acid X]

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2016-2-15-fig1.png

In December 2015, during the investigation of the epidemiological outbreak of hypoglycemic encephalopathy in children in Muzaffarpur (India) experts found unexpectedly that this outbreak was result of not some infection but poisoning by α-amino acid $\mathbf{X}$ ($\ce{C6H9NO2}$) which is present in seeds of lychee fruits. This amino acid significantly decreases the level of sugar in blood up to fatal case. This amino acid was isolated for the first time by British chemists in 1962. Its structure was deduced from the data of its catalytic hydrogenation in the presence of Adams catalyst. Namely, hydrogenation of $\mathbf{X}$ using 1 equivalent of dihydrogen, mixture of two diastereomeric optically active acids $\mathbf{Y1}$ and $\mathbf{Y2}$ is formed. Hydrogenation of $\mathbf{X}$ with two equiv. of $\ce{H2}$ produces the mixture of leucine, norleucine and isoleucine. The structure of $\mathbf{X}$ was assigned unambiguously from $^1$H NMR spectrum, wherein multiplet with the intensity corresponding to two protons is present at 5.7 ppm.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2016-2-15-fig2.png

The synthetic approaches to acid $\mathbf{X}$ were developed much later. Thus, in 2006 in Moscow State University synthesis of racemic diastereomers of $\mathbf{X}$ ($\mathbf{X'}$ in Scheme below) was proposed. The key intermediate $\mathbf{C}$ can be obtained by two different methods. In the first one, the starting compound is methallyl chloride. In the second one, this is methyltriphenylphosphonium iodide.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2016-2-15-fig3.png

1. Decipher structure of amino acid $\mathbf{X}$, point out the absolute configuration of chiral center(s) in terms of $R,S$-nomenclature, propose its name according to IUPAC nomenclature.

2. Write down structural formulae of $\mathbf{Y1}$ and $\mathbf{Y2}$.

3. Decode scheme of synthesis of the mixture of racemic diastereomers $\mathbf{X'}$, if it is know that: a) under normal conditions compound $\mathbf{A'}$ is gaseous; its $^1$H NMR spectrum consists of 2 signals, its $^{13}$C NMR spectrum has 3 signals; b) bicyclic compound $\mathbf{E}$ contains pentacoordinated phosphorus atom; c) compound $\mathbf{G}$ is the derivative of imidazole (five-membered ring containing two nitrogen atoms).

problems.title: [Bacterial biodegradation of PET]
problems.problem:
Problem 1. [Bacterial biodegradation of PET]

"I'll be back"
Terminator T-800

Paying tribute to my constant co-author

Plastic pollution is defined as accumulation of plastic products in the environment producing a negative impact on animal and human habitats. This problem is among the most vital challenges facing humanity nowadays. Surprisingly, sometimes nature itself offers assistance, such as bioremediation. Thus, Japanese researchers have recently discovered that the bacterium Ideonella sakaiensis can use polyethylene terephthalate (PET), a polymer with an extremely high resistance towards biodegradation, as the major source of carbon and energy.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-1-1-fig1.png

PET biodegradation involves two enzymatic steps catalyzed by hydrolases and leading to three low molecular weight ($M<600\,\mathrm{g/mole}$) aromatic products $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, and $\mathbf{C}$ with the number of types of hydrogens of 2, 4, and 6, respectively. After penetration inside Ideonella sakaiensis cells, $\mathbf{C}$ is metabolized into $\mathbf{A}$, which turns out to be the only source of carbon for the bacterium.

1. Show the chemical bonds (use arrows) in the PET formula that are cleaved in the process of its hydrolase-catalyzed biodegradation.

2. Draw all possible structures of $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, and $\mathbf{C}$, which are in agreement with the given data.

$\mathbf{A}$ undergoes a three-step enzyme catalyzed metabolic transformation (all chemical equations):

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-1-1-fig2.png

X is a functional group in $\mathbf{A3}$, $\ce{NADP+}$ and NADPH are oxidized and reduced co-enzyme forms, respectively.

3. Deduce the structural formula of $\mathbf{A3}$ if its molar fractions of oxygen and hydrogen are equal and lower than that of carbon.

4. Draw the structural formulae of $\mathbf{A1}$ and $\mathbf{A2}$.

5. Choose the correct statement concerning Ideonella sakaiensis in the Answer Sheet.

It was reported that the rate of the PET-based film biodegradation by an established bacterial colony with a constant number of cells is of $0.13\,\mathrm{mg\cdot cm^{-2}\cdot days^{-1}}$.

6. Calculate how many days the colony would need to degrade 1 mass% of spherical PET granules with the diameter of 1 cm and density of $1.45\,\mathrm{g\cdot cm^{-3}}$.

The possibility of PET hydrolysis was previously shown for cutinase, the enzyme involved in nature in a similar process of degradation of the biopolymer cutin, which is the major component of cuticle covering plant leaves. The compound $\mathbf{D}$ (70.54% C, 11.84% H, and 17.62% O by mass) is the major monomer in cutin biosynthesis.

7. Deduce the structure of $\mathbf{D}$ ($M < 300\,\mathrm{g/mole}$) if it is an unbranched compound free of chiral carbon atoms.

8. Draw the monomer unit of the polymer composed solely of $\mathbf{D}$.

problems.title: [A non-proteinogenic amino acid with a strongly acidic group]
problems.problem:
Problem 2. [A non-proteinogenic amino acid with a strongly acidic group]

Proteins are composed of α-amino acid residues linked together by peptide bonds between carboxylic and amino groups. Alongside such canonical (proteinogenic) α-amino acids, there are other natural compounds containing amino and acidic groups. Being involved in metabolic processes, the latter substances are not found in proteins. Thus, the compound $\mathbf{A}$ with the molar mass of 125 g/mole is used as a drug and nutritional supplement. It reveals much more pronounced acidic properties than those of α-amino acids.

1. Give one example of each of optically inactive and optically active canonical α-amino acids. Draw the latter as a Fischer projection of the isomer incorporated into proteins during biosynthesis. Indicate the absolute configuration (R/S) of the asymmetric center.

$\mathbf{A}$ is a white crystalline powder readily soluble in water and poorly in most organic solvents. Values of the acidity constants $pK_a$ of the acidic and ammonium groups in $\mathbf{A}$ equals 1.50 and 8.74, respectively, whereas there are no other ionogenic groups in $\mathbf{A}$.

2. Write down expressions for the acidity constants. Denote the neutral form of $\mathbf{A}$ as HA, and the acidity constants as $K_1 = K_a(\ce{H2A+})$ and $K_2 = K_a(\mathrm{HA})$.

3. Show the prevailing form of an amino acid at its isoelectric point (the total charge of all the amino acid forms equals zero) using alanine (2-aminopropionic acid) as an example.

4. Calculate the pH value of the $\mathbf{A}$ solution at its isoelectric point.

5. What is the molar fraction of the completely uncharged form of $\mathbf{A}$ in the above solution if ionization of the ionogenic groups in $\mathbf{A}$ occurs independently?

The antimicrobial compound $\mathbf{X}$ was first synthesized from $\mathbf{A}$ according to the hereunder scheme:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-1-2-fig1.png

6. Draw the structural formulae of $\mathbf{A}$ – $\mathbf{D}$.

$\mathbf{A}$ is very important for mammals. Most of them are capable of biosynthesizing it form an α-amino acid $\mathbf{E}$ in three consecutive enzymatic steps (enzymes $\mathrm{E_1}$ – $\mathrm{E_3}$) given hereunder. The process includes only decarboxylation and two-electron oxidation reactions. Still, $\mathbf{A}$ is an indispensible substance for some mammals because of low decarbolylase activity, which terminates the synthesis at the second step and makes the presence of $\mathbf{A}$ in the diet obligatory.

$$\mathbf{E} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{E_1}} \mathbf{F} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{E_2}} \mathbf{G} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{E_3}} \mathbf{A}$$

7. Write down the three-step scheme of the $\mathbf{A}$ biosynthesis showing the structures of the intermediates and starting amino acid $\mathbf{E}$.

$\mathbf{A}$ was first time isolated as its sodium salt from bovine bile. $\mathbf{A}$ interacts with bile acids (cholic, in particular) providing conjugates, which act as surfactants facilitating emulsification of fats in intestinal track. In liver, cholic acid combines with glycine and $\mathbf{A}$ affording $\mathbf{H}$ and $\mathbf{I}$, respectively.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-1-2-fig2.png

8. Draw the structural formulae of $\mathbf{H}$ and $\mathbf{I}$. Which of these is a more potent emulsifier of fats? Choose the molecule and encircle the functional group responsible for the enhanced emulsifying ability.

Alkene oxidation reactions belong to the most widespread methods of C–C double bond functionalization in the organic synthesis.

Sharpless developed an enantioselective epoxidation of allylic alcohols based on the use of t-BuOOH as an oxidant and $\mathbf{Me}(\mathrm{OR})_n$ as a catalyst. 5. Determine the formula of alcoholate $\mathbf{Me}(\mathrm{OR})_n$ if spectrum $^1$H NMR contains two signals (doublet and septet with the relative intensity of 6:1), and $\omega_\mathrm{C} = 50.7\%$.

To determine a major enantiomer of oxirane, formed in the above reaction, the Sharpless rule is applied. According to this rule, molecule of allyl alcohol derivative is presented by way given below. Problem 5. [Ladderanes]

Ladderanes form very interesting class of hydrocarbons, unusual structural fragment of which is present in the Nature in lipids of planctomycetes that realize anammox, i.e. ANaerobic AMMonium OXidation. The molecular formula of [2]-ladderane, the simplest representative of this class, is $\ce{C6H10}$. This compound can be produced in low yield by photolysis of norbornan-2-one or 1,5-hexadiene.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-1-5-fig1.png

1. Write down structural formula of [2]-ladderane if it is known that: a) it has no free rotating bonds; b) its $^1$H NMR spectrum consists of 3 signals, c) two signals are present in its $^{13}$C NMR spectrum. Write name of [2]-ladderane using IUPAC nomenclature.

Molecular formula of [3]-ladderane is $\ce{C8H12}$; it has two stereoisomers: anti-[3]-ladderane, having one plane of symmetry, and syn-[3]-ladderane, having two planes of symmetry. Both isomers were synthesized from cis-3,4-dichlorocyclobut-1-ene. Its treatment with sodium amalgam produces very active intermediate $\mathbf{A}$ ($\ce{C4H4}$) which dimerizes immediately affording compound $\mathbf{B}$. The catalytic hydrogenation of $\mathbf{B}$ yields syn-[3]-ladderane. On the another hand, treatment of cis-3,4-dichlorocyclobut-1-ene with lithium amalgam gives rise to organolithium compound $\mathbf{C}$ ($\ce{LiC8H8Cl}$) which spontaneously eliminate lithium chloride with formation of hydrocarbon $\mathbf{D}$, the catalytic hydrogenation of which accomplishes synthesis of anti-[3]-ladderane.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-1-5-fig2.png

2. Decipher structures of [3]-ladderanes. Write down structural formulae of compounds $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{D}$ as well as reactive intermediates $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{C}$.

3. Write down the general structural formula of [n]-ladderanes no accounting for stereochemistry of these compounds.

Anaerobic bacteria Candidatus Brocadia anammoxidans use the transformation of $\ce{NO2^-}$ and $\ce{NH4+}$ into $\ce{N2}$ and $\ce{H2O}$ as the source of energy. This process proceeds in organelle that has very unusual membrane: 90% of lipid component of this membrane is formed by pentacycloanammoxic acid, $\ce{C20H30O2}$. The key structural element of this acid is [5]-ladderane which has only anti-arrangement of rings. It is also known that this acid has 9 tertiary carbon atoms, has no quaternary carbons; carbon atom of the ladderane scaffold, bearing a substituent, has (S)-configuration.

4. Write down structural formula of pentacycloanammoxic acid.

problems.title: [Two metals discovered by Davy]
problems.problem:
Problem 6. [Two metals discovered by Davy]

It was a serious breakthrough in chemistry with the discovery of electricity: the birth of electrochemistry, the discovery of new elements, etc. In 1807 Humphry Davy obtained the metals $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ by electrolysis of their molten compounds. The reactivity of these elements is incomparable, thus, being on the air, they quickly turn into a mixture of oxides, peroxides, nitrides, carbonates and others.

H. Davy (1778 – 1829)

problems.title: [Portland cement clinker]
problems.problem:
Problem 7. [Portland cement clinker]

There are many types of cement, but the most widespread one is Portland cement. It is mostly (more than 90%) composed of ground clinker, whose approximate composition is given in the table below. The properties of Portland cement are commonly defined by two calcium silicates, $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$, in the clinker. The mass fractions of calcium in $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ are 52.66% and 46.54% respectively. The first row of the table below contains the international designations (in cement chemistry) of various components of the clinker. In reality, clinker comprises approximately 2–3% mass. of minor components (oxides of potassium, sodium, phosphorus, manganese, sulfur, hydrogen, etc. in bound states, which come from the source materials), but we will not consider them in this problem.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c} \text{Designation} & & & \mathbf{C_4AF} & \mathbf{C_3A} & \mathbf{M} \\ \hline \text{Composition} & \mathbf{X} & \mathbf{Y} & \ce{Ca4Al2Fe2O10} & \ce{Ca3Al2O6} & \ce{MgO} \\ \hline \omega,\% & 62.0 & 16.0 & 8.50 & 12.0 & 1.50 \end{array}$$

The raw materials used in making the clinker are various natural minerals: limestone (calcite), clay (kaolinite $\ce{Al2O3*2SiO2*2H2O}$), periclase (MgO), iron ore ($\ce{Fe2O3}$) and quartz sand. All the aforementioned minerals contain $\ce{SiO2}$ as an impurity, which is 8.50% of the minerals by mass. In addition to $\ce{SiO2}$, iron ore also contains 4.10% of $\ce{Al2O3}$, and clay contains 4.60% of $\ce{Fe2O3}$. All the starting materials are mixed together in required proportions and calcined (heated when exposed to air) at $1500\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ in special rotating furnaces to obtain clinker. After cooling and grinding, the clinker is mixed with gypsum (under these conditions, it partially dehydrates to form gypsum plaster, also known as plaster of Paris) to produce Portland cement. The amount of gypsum added must be so that the mass fraction of sulfur oxide (VI) in the final product is 3.00%.

Because the compositions of natural raw materials used in the process are not constant in a real industrial process, the ratios of the components used in making clinker must constantly be adjusted. The properties of Portland cement are most affected by the ratio of $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$, which depends on the ratio of $\ce{SiO2}$, $\ce{Al2O3}$ and $\ce{Fe2O3}$ in the clinker. In order to control this ratio, the Lime Saturation Factor (LSF) is used, which is computed by using the mass fractions of the aforementioned oxides in the clinker. The Lime Saturation Factor is computed as follows:

$$\mathrm{LSF} = \frac{\omega(\ce{CaO})}{2.80\cdot\omega(\ce{SiO2}) + 1.18\cdot\omega(\ce{Al2O3}) + 0.650\cdot\omega(\ce{Fe2O3})}$$

The LSF characterizes the ratio between quantities of $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$, as well as the degree of binding of CaO in the clinker. If LSF = 1, then only $\mathbf{X}$ is present and there is no $\mathbf{Y}$, and if LSF>1, then $\mathbf{X}$ and unbound CaO are present. The magnitude of LSF is used to confirm that the composition of cement is standardized, and will behave in a predictable manner.

1. Determine the chemical formulas of X and Y and give their international designations.

2. Calculate the masses of all components needed to produce 100 tons of Portland cement.

3. Calculate the mass fractions of all oxides in Portland cement.

4. Calculate LSF for Portland cement of the above composition. Show your calculations.

In all calculations, use atomic masses rounded to the nearest integer. The final answers should have at least three significant figures.

problems.title: [Photocatalytic water splitting on titanium dioxide]
problems.problem:
Problem 8. [Photocatalytic water splitting on titanium dioxide]

Hydrogen is a promising renewable energy source. One of the ways of production of hydrogen is photocatalytic decomposition of water. The mechanism of the process is presented in figure. Titanium dioxide can serve as an example of such a photo-catalyst. Under light excitation with photon energy, greater than the band gap of the semiconductor ($E_\mathrm{g}$) electrons transfer to the conduction band, leaving holes (h+) in the valence band. The efficiency of the process decreases because of rapid recombination of the pairs $\mathrm{e^-}$–$\mathrm{h^+}$. For charge separation the catalyst is doped by transition metals.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-1-8-fig1.png

1. Choose the metals in the table, addition of which can improve the efficiency of photo-catalytic decomposition of water.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{Ion} & E^0(\ce{Me^{n+}}/\ce{Me}),\ \mathrm{V} & \text{Ion} & E^0(\ce{Me^{n+}}/\ce{Me}),\ \mathrm{V} \\ \hline \ce{Fe^{3+}} & -0.037 & \ce{Pt^{2+}} & 1.12 \\ \hline \ce{Mn^{2+}} & -1.19 & \ce{Ru^{2+}} & 0.445 \\ \hline \ce{Co^{2+}} & -0.28 & \ce{Cu^{2+}} & 0.521 \\ \hline \ce{Ce^{3+}} & -2.34 & \ce{Ag+} & 0.7996 \end{array}$$

In the systems, having particles smaller than 100 nm, size effects are often observed – dependence of physical-chemical properties of substances from the size of the particles. Dependence of the band gap on the size of nanoparticles for an oxide semiconductor is expressed by the formula

$$E_\mathrm{g}(R) = E_\mathrm{g0} + \frac{a}{R^2} - \frac{b}{R},$$

where $E_\mathrm{g0}$ – band gap of the bulk phase, $\mu = m_\mathrm{e}^*\cdot m_\mathrm{h}^*/(m_\mathrm{e}^* + m_\mathrm{h}^*)$ – reduced mass of the effective masses of electron ($m_\mathrm{e}^*$) and a hole ($m_\mathrm{h}^*$), $\varepsilon_0$ – electric constant, $\varepsilon$ – dielectric permittivity, $e$ – electron charge, $R$ – radius of the particle, $a = h^2/8\mu$, $b = 1.8e^2/4\pi\varepsilon\varepsilon_0$.

2. a) Calculate the band gap energy value for $\ce{TiO2}$ nanoparticles with $R = 2\,\mathrm{nm}$, if $E_\mathrm{g0} = 3.0\,\mathrm{eV}$, $\varepsilon = 184$, $\mu = 0.74\,m_\mathrm{e}$; b) In what direction shifts the wavelength of radiation which initiates conductivity, in case of nanoparticles, compared with bulk phase? c) Calculate the effective mass of electrons and holes if $m_\mathrm{e}^* = 12.5\,m_\mathrm{h}^*$.

Efficiency of photocatalytic hydrogen production can be estimated with the quantum yield $\varphi$ – ratio of the number of the "effective" electrons ($n_\mathrm{e}$) to the number of photons ($n_\mathrm{p}$) generated by a light source per time unit.

3. Calculate the quantum yield $n_\mathrm{e}/n_\mathrm{p}$ (%). The maximum rate of hydrogen formation for this catalyst $V_\mathrm{max} = 5.6\,\mathrm{\mu mol/min}$, light source power $P = 67\,\mathrm{mW}$, light wavelength 421 nm.

Kinetics of the reactions, occurring on the photocatalyst surface, can be described using Langmuir – Hinshelwood model:

$$\ce{A + Z <=>[K_A] AZ ->[k] P + Z}$$

where Z – adsorption centers, A – organic substrate, P – product of the reaction, $K_\mathrm{A}$ – adsorption constant, $k$ – reaction rate constant. The rate of hydrogen in this reaction is defined as $W(\ce{H2}) = kn_\mathrm{A}$, where $n_\mathrm{A} = \dfrac{K_\mathrm{A}C_\mathrm{0A}}{1 + K_\mathrm{A}C_\mathrm{0A}}$ – degree of surface coverage. After linearization of the curve $W(\ce{H2})$ the equation $y = 3.27 + 1.78x$ was obtained (see figure).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-1-8-fig2.png

4. a) Determine, to what variables correspond $x$ and $y$ on the graph; b) calculate $k$ and $K_\mathrm{A}$.

Physical constants: $h = 6.63\cdot10^{-34}\,\mathrm{J\cdot s}$, $N_\mathrm{A} = 6.02\cdot10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$, $c = 3\cdot10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\cdot s^{-1}}$, $1\,\mathrm{eV} = 1.6\cdot10^{-19}\,\mathrm{J}$, $m_\mathrm{e} = 9.1\cdot10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}$, $\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\cdot10^{-12}\,\mathrm{F/m}$, $e = 1.6\cdot10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$.

Problem 2 (Inorganic Chemistry section, problem 2). [Dodecahydrododecaborate and carborane superacids]

The most compounds containing the chemical bond B–H have a high reactivity. However, there are exceptions to this rule. In 1955 on the basis of theoretical calculations it was shown that dodecahydrododecaborate(2–) anion and isoelectronic structures should be high stable. Formally, this anion can be considered a derivative of a non-existent dodecaboran (14). In 1960, the corresponding salt of sodium dodecahydrododecaborate(2–) was first obtained, which really had enviable stability. The matter turned out to be in the spatial structure of an anion having a regular highly symmetric structure. All the boron atoms in it are located at the vertices of the regular polyhedron with 12 vertices (icosahedron), and each of the 20 faces is an equilateral triangle with boron atoms at its vertices. It is believed that the icosahedron of boron atoms and isoelectronic structures have spatial aromaticity and this explains their high stability.

1. Give the formulas and names of three really existing substances, the molecules of which have a spatial framework, which is a polyhedron, in the vertices of which atoms of one chemical element connected by chemical bonds are located.

2. Calculate the multiplicity of each chemical bond in the dodecahydrododecaborate (2–) anion.

The dodecahydododecaborate (2–) anion is not destroyed at $95\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ in concentrated aqueous solutions of alkali (NaOH) and acids (HCl). The corresponding acid (A) isolated from the aqueous solution is slightly stronger than sulfuric acid.

3. Calculate the mass fraction of boron in acid A, give your calculations.

To obtain the sodium dodecahydrododecaborate(2–) can be as follows. In the first step, sodium octahydrotriborate(1–) is obtained from sodium tetrahydroborate(1–) and diborane (6). In the second step the pyrolysis of the product at $180\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is carried out and the final product is obtained.

4. Draw the structural formula of the anion product of the first step synthesis.

5. Give the reaction equations for the preparation of sodium dodecahydrododecaborate(2–).

If in the dodecahydrododecaborate(2–) anion one boron atom is replaced by a carbon atom without disturbing the three-dimensional aromaticity of the system, a very stable anion (B) is obtained, which made it possible to synthesize one of the most powerful superacids (C) at the present time. To produce it, the anion B (as a cesium salt) is first chlorinated with an excess of $\ce{SO2Cl2}$ (in argon atmosphere) in a suitable solvent, whereby all hydrogen atoms in the B-H bonds are replaced by chlorine atoms. The obtaining salt can be converted to a superacid (C), called carborane acid, as a result of several additional steps.

6. Give the formula of carborane acid C.

Carborane acid is capable of protonating methane at room temperature. In this case, its solid stable salt is formed with methyl carbocation. When this salt is washed on the filter with cyclohexane at room temperature, the product is contaminated with another solid salt.

7. Give a scheme of the reaction proceeding at hexane washing and explain the structure of the salt, which is formed.

In 2013, the super acid D was obtained even more strongly than carborane.

8. What is the mass fraction of boron in D? Show your calculations.

(The nomenclature of boron compounds with hydrogen includes the designation of the number of boron atoms in the Latin numerals with the addition of borane and the addition at the end in parentheses of the Arabic number of hydrogen atoms, for example, $\ce{B4H10}$ – tetraborane(10). For anions the number of hydrogen atoms and the number of boron atoms indicate with the addition of borate, and the charge of the anion indicates in parentheses at the end. Problem 3 (Inorganic Chemistry section, problem 3). [Binary compounds of two elements X and Y]

Two chemical elements ($\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$) combine to form different binary compounds, which could be gases, liquids or even solids. Nine of these binary compounds ($\mathbf{A}$ – $\mathbf{I}$) are descripted on this scheme:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-3-fig1.png

The treatment of compound $\mathbf{A}$ by the solution of sodium hypochlorite (Raschig processes) is used to obtain colorless liquid $\mathbf{B}$, which it is not possible to obtain by the direct interaction of simple compounds of $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$. This liquid $\mathbf{B}$ is mostly used as a racket fuel. $\mathbf{B}$ could be obtained from the white compound $\mathbf{K}$: the reaction of 0.72 g of $\mathbf{K}$ with the excess of sodium hypochlorite solution, gives 0.384 g of liquid $\mathbf{B}$. The hydrolysis of the compound $\mathbf{K}$ produces two gases $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{W}$ ($\rho_\mathbf{W} = 1{,}964\,\mathrm{g/L}$ at the normal conditions). The volatile and caustic liquid $\mathbf{C}$ was obtained for the first time by the reaction of $\mathbf{B}$ with the acid $\mathbf{L}$. The using of excess of the acid $\mathbf{L}$ leads to the further oxidation of compound $\mathbf{C}$ with the formation of equimolar quantities of gases $\mathbf{Y}$, $\mathbf{Z}$ and water. The compound $\mathbf{C}$ is a basic when reacts with strong acids (for example the formation of salt $\mathbf{M}$) or it is an acid when reacts with the compounds $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ giving salts $\mathbf{D}$ and $\mathbf{E}$ respectively. For synthesis of 0.855 g of the salt $\mathbf{E}$ by the sequences $\mathbf{B} \rightarrow \mathbf{C} \rightarrow \mathbf{E}$, 0.864 g of compound $\mathbf{B}$ have to be used taking into account that the yield on two stages is respectively 80% and 95%. By gradual heating at low pressure the unstable compound $\mathbf{F}$ could be obtained from the liquid $\mathbf{C}$. The compound $\mathbf{F}$ transforms to the yellow gas $\mathbf{G}$ and reacting with oxygen forms the acid $\mathbf{L}$ even at the room temperature. The compound $\mathbf{F}$ could exist in the singlet and triplet states. The compound $\mathbf{H}$ was never obtained in a pure state, but it exists as salt $\mathbf{H}\cdot\mathrm{HCl}$ and it is a side product of Raschig processes. The compound $\mathbf{H}\cdot\mathrm{HCl}$ is the only product of the reaction $\mathbf{B}+\mathbf{J}$. The covalent compound $\mathbf{I}$ is the derivative of the compound $\mathbf{G}$, which exists in different isomeric forms. The heating of $\mathbf{I}$ leads to the isomerization reaction giving the salt $\mathbf{D}$, or to the formation of $\mathbf{B}$ with emission of one equivalent of gas $\mathbf{Y}$. The compounds $\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{H}$ are similar structurally.

1. Decipher binary compounds $\mathbf{A}$ – $\mathbf{I}$ and also compounds $\mathbf{J}$ – $\mathbf{M}$, $\mathbf{W}$, $\mathbf{X}$ – $\mathbf{Z}$.

2. Write the equations of all described reactions.

3. Write Lewis structures for singlet and triplet states of compound $\mathbf{F}$. Give a particle (molecule or atom) which is isoelectronic to $\mathbf{F}$.

4. Why $\mathbf{H}\cdot\mathrm{HCl}$ could be a side product during the Raschig processes? Write down the equation of this chemical reaction.

Problem 6 (Organic Chemistry section, problem 3). [Synthesis of pentacycloanammoxic acid]

Pentacycloanammoxic acid is component of phospholipid $\mathbf{1}$ forming membrane of anammoxosome (organelle wherein anammox proceeds). Anammox (ANaerobic AMMonium OXidation) is globally important microbial process of the nitrogen cycle. This process ($\ce{NH4+ + NO2^- -> N2 + 2H2O}$) is very slow and includes toxic $\ce{N2H4}$ and $\ce{NH2OH}$, as well as reactive radicals as intermediates. This is why anammoxosome membrane is formed by so unusual phospholipids that prevent diffusion of these toxic intermediates into the cell. In 2004–2006 Corey and co-workers synthesized pentacycloanammoxic acid in both racemic and optically active forms. However, these syntheses do not provide to prepare this interesting compound in gram quantities. Only in 2016, group from Stanford University developed the preparative method for the synthesis of such compounds including lipid $\mathbf{1}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-6-fig1.png

The key to the success of this synthesis was the development of multi-gram approach to [5]-ladderane based on dimerization of hydrocarbon $\mathbf{F}$ (scheme 2). Among further steps it is needed to point out enantioselective hydroboration of hydrocarbon $\mathbf{H}$ followed by Zweifel coupling ($\mathbf{I}$-to-$\mathbf{J}$ step). The sequence of transformation during this coupling is given in Scheme 1 using a general example of reaction between chiral organoboron compound, vinylmagnesium bromide and iodine.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-6-fig2.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-6-fig3.png
