1. Write down structural formulae of compounds $\mathbf{A}$-$\mathbf{K}$ if it is known that:

• $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{H}$ have plane of symmetry
• compound $\mathbf{D}$ can exist in two diastereomeric forms; both diastereomers have plane of symmetry
• compound $\mathbf{E}$ can exist in four diastereomeric forms; all diastereomers are chiral.

2. Propose structures of intermediates $\mathbf{X1}$ and $\mathbf{X2}$ as well as mechanism for further transformation of $\mathbf{X2}$.

3. Propose evolutionary factor(s) influenced the emerging of this unusual type of ladderane membranes of anammoxosomes in the Nature (point out right answer in the list given).

a) highly reactive intermediates of anammox catalyze biosynthesis of ladderanes;

b) ladderane skeleton allows for formation of ultradense membranes;

c) highly reactive anammox intermediates are starting compounds in ladderanes biosynthesis;

d) ladderane can react with highly reactive intermediates of anammox.

problems.title: [Wine flavour: glycosides, resveratrol and a ketose]
problems.problem:
Problem 7 (Life Sciences and Polymers section, problem 1). [Wine flavour: glycosides, resveratrol and a ketose]

Wine flavor and properties are mostly predetermined during the yeast fermentation of wine materials. Carbohydrates known to be the major source for ethanol production and thus recognized as the key substances in fermentation are also involved in the formation of glycosides. The latter are molecules in which a sugar residue is bound to another molecule residue (known as aglycone) via a glycosidic bond.

An alcohol $\mathbf{X}$ (13.10% O by mass) is behind the flavor of vintage wines and cognacs. It can be formed from the amino acid L-phenylalanine via three enzymatic steps (decarboxylation, reduction, and transamination given in an arbitrary order) and from sugars.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-7-fig1.png

In wines $\mathbf{X}$ exists in the form of its glycoside with D-glucose.

1. Draw the Haworth projection of D-glucopyranoside of $\mathbf{X}$. Use R- for the aglycone.

Usually glycosides are easily hydrolyzed by acids, but not by alkalis. However, under aqueous alkali treatment D-glucoside of $\mathbf{X}$ affords the aglycone and an extremely stable substance $\mathbf{X0}$ with the molecular formula coinciding with the empirical one of starch.

2. Draw the most stable chair conformer of $\mathbf{X0}$.

3. Deduce the composition and draw the structures of $\mathbf{X}$, $\mathbf{X1}$, and $\mathbf{X2}$, if all of these contain oxygen, whereas phenylalanine is the only chiral compound in the reaction sequence.

Flavonoid aglycones such as resveratrol are assumed to possess antioxidant and cancer preventative properties. Such aglycones are also formed from sugars:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-7-fig2.png

Malonyl-CoA is a typical two-carbon source in biosynthesis:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-7-fig3.png

4. Draw the structure of $\mathbf{Y}$.

5. Propose the structure of $\mathbf{Z}$ if it contains three six-membered rings formed as a result of Claisen condensation of $\mathbf{Y}$ followed by intramolecular Michael addition.

6. How many D-glucopyranosides of resveratrol are possible?

Excessive content of ketose $\mathbf{A}$ in the wine material may adversely affect the flavor of the beverage. $\mathbf{A}$ formation during the fermentation of grape juice occurs in a single enzymatic step from metabolite $\mathbf{B}$. The reaction is carried out by Acetobacteraceae bacteria, which gets energy from a two-step oxidation of ethanol to acetic acid with acetaldehyde as an intermediate.

7. Deduce and draw the structures of $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$, if their hydrogen mass content differs by 2.05%.

8. $\mathbf{A}$ exists as a cyclic dimer in the crystalline state. Draw the structure of this dimer.

problems.title: [miR-122, miravirsen and an expanded genetic alphabet]
problems.problem:
Problem 8 (Life Sciences and Polymers section, problem 2). [miR-122, miravirsen and an expanded genetic alphabet]

MicroRNA are small non-coding RNA molecules composed of 18-25 nucleotide residues and found in plants, animals and some viruses. miR-122 is the prevailing microRNA in liver cells. There it regulates energy production and lipid metabolism as well as facilitates replication of hepatitis C (HCV) virus, which negatively influences the disease prognosis. The nucleotide sequence of miR-122 is:

5'-UGGAGUGUGACAAUGGUGUUUGU-3'

Two miR-122 molecules must interact with the hereunder fragment of the viral genome to potentiate the HCV amplification. It was discovered that one of these miR-122 molecules forms 10 nucleotide pairs (3 sequential pairs at the first site and 7 sequential pairs at the second site, that is 3+7), whereas the second one forms 9 pairs (3+6).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-8-fig1.png

1. Determine the direction of the miR-122 chains attached to the HCV RNA fragment.

2. In the Answer Sheet, underline the nucleotides in the miR-122 molecules involved in coupling with the HCV RNA fragment. Note that RNA molecules can form loops bringing together nucleotides that are far apart in the primary structure (for instance, see the above fragment of the HCV genome).

Miravirsen is an experimental drug for the treatment of viral hepatitis C. The substance blocks the HCV replication by binding with miR-122. Miravirsen is composed of 15 nucleotide residues linked to each other by phosphodiester bonds between 3' and 5' C atoms. If counted from one of the molecule ends, 2'-deoxythymidines are found at the 3rd, 9th, 11th and 12th positions. All the 15 nucleotide residues of miravirsen consecutively (without loops and omissions) bind to a fragment of miR-122.

3. Draw a single strain DNA, which, being a miravirsen analog, binds with exactly the same RNA fragment of miR-122 as the drug does.

Beside 2'-deoxynucleotide residues, miravirsen contains locked nucleotides (LNA). The ribose moiety and phosphate residues of the latter are modified as compared to their natural analogs. Thus, the compound $\mathbf{Z}$ with the molecular formula of $\ce{C11H14N5O6SP}$ contains 4 cycles. Being an adenosine-5'-monophosphate analog, $\mathbf{Z}$ belongs to the LNA class. Derivatives of the hereunder substance play the key role in the laboratory synthesis of $\mathbf{Z}$:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-8-fig2.png

4. Deduce the structure of $\mathbf{Z}$. Note that $\mathbf{Z}$-based RNA is much more resistant towards hydrolysis than a natural one.

5. Indicate which method of miravirsen administration is least favorable.

A DNA duplex can also be modified. In 2014, researchers from University of California, San Diego have designed the first living thing (originating from E.coli) with 6 nitrogenous bases. A synthetic $\mathbf{X}$-$\mathbf{Y}$ pair supplemented two conventional A–T and G–C ones.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-8-fig3.png

6. How many hydrogen bonds do exist in the complementary $\mathbf{X}$-$\mathbf{Y}$ pair within the duplex of the semi-synthetic DNA?

In 2016, the researchers introduced changes in the nucleotides transporter and obtained a colony of semi-synthetic bacteria containing $\mathbf{X}$–$\mathbf{Y}$ pair, which underwent replication with high accuracy, was presumed and inherited. The improvements became possible due to introduction of a diatom Phaeodactylum tricornutum gene into E.coli genome. The gene encodes the NTT protein, which is very efficient in transporting $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ containing nucleotides from nutrient medium into the cell.

7. Deduce the structure of the substance $\mathbf{W}$ (15.00% P and 31.01% O by mass), which, being an $\mathbf{X}$ metabolite, was added to the nutrient medium and then efficiently transported by the NTT protein inside E.coli.

problems.title: [Polymeric micelles for paclitaxel delivery]
problems.problem:
Problem 9 (Life Sciences and Polymers section, problem 3). [Polymeric micelles for paclitaxel delivery]

State-of-art chemistry allows designing drugs highly efficient at both molecular and cellular level. However, lack of target delivery of biologically active molecules often hinders the resulting effect. Thus, many promising drugs are poorly soluble in water, which makes attaining therapeutical concentrations (i.g., $\mathrm{IC_{50}}$) in body impossible. For instance, the solubility of an anti-cancer remedy Paclitaxel ($M = 854\,\mathrm{g/mole}$) in water is as low as 6.7 mg/L. Use of amphiphilic polymers capable of small (up to 50 nm) micelles formation is one of the options. Polymers with high drug-loading capacity $LC = 45\%$. ($LC = m_\mathrm{drug}/(m_\mathrm{drug} + m_\mathrm{polymer})\cdot100\%$, where $m_\mathrm{drug}$ and $m_\mathrm{polymer}$ are the drug and polymer masses in the solution, respectively) have been recently developed (see the hereunder scheme):

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-9-fig1.png

The polymer shown in the scheme was obtained by co-polymerization of heterocyclic compounds $\mathbf{A1}$ – $\mathbf{A3}$ belonging to one and the same class. These compounds can be prepared by the interaction of corresponding nitriles (R–CN, $\mathrm{R^1}$ = Me, $\mathrm{R^2}$ = n-Bu, $\mathrm{R^3}$ = $\ce{CH2Ph}$) with $\ce{H2N-CH2CH2-OH}$ mediated by $\ce{Cd(CH3COO)2*2H2O}$. The structure of the parent polymer obtained from the simplest heterocyclic monomer ($\mathbf{A}$) of the class (end groups omitted) is shown hereunder:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-9-fig2.png

1. Draw the structures of $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{A1}$ – $\mathbf{A3}$.

Cationic polymerization of monomers of $\mathbf{A}$ class proceeds via «living chains» mechanism, i.e. active centers are infinitely long retained in the system when the entire monomer is consumed, whereas addition of new portions of monomer(s) re-initializes the polymerization process. Co-polymers $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ were obtained according to the hereunder scheme (all polymerization steps were conducted till complete consumption of corresponding monomer(s)).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-9-fig3.png

2. Draw the structures of co-polymers $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$, clearly showing the degree of polymerization and terminal groups.

3. Draw the reactive intermediate formed upon $\mathbf{A}$ interaction with TsOMe. Use the intermediate structure to demonstrate the mechanism of the cationic polymerization. Note that the reactive intermediate exists in solution in two equilibrium forms (cyclic and acyclic).

4. Calculate the molar ratio of $\mathbf{P}$ and Paclitaxel in the micelle.

5. Calculate the Paclitaxel solubility in water in the presence of $\mathbf{P}$ if it is known that the saturated micellar solution achieves $\mathrm{IC_{50}} = 0.37\,\mathrm{nmol/L}$ (for cancer cell lines PC3) at $17.7\cdot10^{6}$ dilution.

6. Calculate the increase factor of Paclitaxel solubility in water when $\mathbf{P}$ is present in the system.

7. Critical micelle concentration (concentration of a polymer above which micelles form) of $\mathbf{P}$ is of $4.4\,\mathrm{\mu mol/L}$. Estimate the standard free Gibbs energy of micelle formation for 1 mole of $\mathbf{P}$.

problems.title: [Determination of bismuth]
problems.problem:
Problem 10 (Analytical Chemistry section, problem 1). [Determination of bismuth]

To determine the concentration of bismuth, 25.0 mL of an acidified $\ce{Bi^{3+}}$ solution were mixed with 20 mL of chloroform, methyltimol blue as indicator was added and the mixture was titrated with a standard ammonium oxalate solution (reaction $\mathbf{A}$) with shaking the flask after addition of each portion of the titrant. Upon addition of 14.36 mL 0.1000 M oxalate solution, the blue color of the suspension changed into green, which could be observed after phase separation. It is given that 1.000 mL of the oxalate solution corresponds to 13.93 mg of Bi.

1. Write down reaction $\mathbf{A}$, indicating the insoluble product formed in it.

2. Confirm the composition of the product by calculation.

3. Calculate the concentration of $\ce{Bi^{3+}}$ in the analyzed solution in mol/L and g/L.

4. When methyltimol blue indicator is added to the solution containing the bismuth salt, a blue complex is formed (reaction $\mathbf{B}$): $\ce{Bi^{3+} + Ind^{3-} = BiInd}$. Explain the principle of this metalchromic indicator by writing down the reaction of this complex with an excess of titrant (reaction $\mathbf{C}$). Which of the substances formed in the reaction is yellow? Underline it.

Lower concentrations of bismuth were determined by adding KBr to 100.0 mL of the test solution so that the precipitate forming at the beginning (reaction $\mathbf{D}$) could completely dissolve (reaction $\mathbf{E}$) forming a slightly yellow solution. The resulting solution was neutralized with sodium hydroxide until faint turbidity, not disappearing on stirring (reaction $\mathbf{F}$); then hexaammine chromium(III) nitrate solution was added for the quantitative precipitation of a bismuth compound (reaction $\mathbf{G}$). The precipitate was filtered off, washed with KBr solution and quantitatively washed off with hot water. While doing that, the precipitate was hydrolyzed to form an insoluble bismuth compound (reaction $\mathbf{H}$). To the resulting suspension, an excess of NaOH was added and heated (reaction $\mathbf{J}$ with the chromium compound); the releasing ammonia was absorbed by a boric acid solution (reaction $\mathbf{K}$). The solution in the receiver was titrated 0.1000 M HCl in the presence of methyl orange (reaction $\mathbf{L}$); 17.2 mL of acid was required.

5. Write down the reactions $\mathbf{D}$ – $\mathbf{L}$. Underline which substance precipitates in reactions $\mathbf{D}$ and $\mathbf{H}$. Circle the yellow substance in reaction $\mathbf{E}$.

6. Calculate the concentration of $\ce{Bi^{3+}}$ in the initial solution in mol/L.

problems.title: [Iron for aquarium plants]
problems.problem:
Problem 11 (Analytical Chemistry section, problem 2). [Iron for aquarium plants]

Vasya's hobby is keeping an aquarium (pH 7.2, dissolved oxygen concentration $3.12\cdot10^{-4}\,\mathrm{M}$). He read in a book that his aquatic plants demand some soluble form of iron and its optimal concentration is $c(\mathrm{Fe}) = 2\,\mathrm{\mu M}$.

For reference: solubility product of $\ce{Fe(OH)3}$ $K_\mathrm{s} = [\ce{Fe^{3+}}][\ce{OH-}]^3 = 4\cdot10^{-38}$; at pH 7.2 the molar fraction of complex-forming ion of EDTA ($\ce{Y^{4-}}$) equals $8\cdot10^{-4}$; equilibrium constant of the reaction $\ce{Fe^{2+} + 1/4O2 + 1/2H2O = Fe^{3+} + OH-}$ in aqueous solution is $K = 10^{5}$; the parameters of the complexes formed by iron ions are as follows:

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c} \text{Complex} & \ce{Fe^{2+}Y} & \ce{Fe^{3+}Y} & \ce{Fe(OH)^{2+}} & \ce{Fe(OH)2+} & \ce{Fe(OH)3} \\ \hline \text{Stability constant} & \beta^\mathrm{II} = \dfrac{[\ce{FeY^{2-}}]}{[\ce{Fe^{2+}}][\ce{Y^{4-}}]} & \beta^\mathrm{III} = \dfrac{[\ce{FeY-}]}{[\ce{Fe^{3+}}][\ce{Y^{4-}}]} & \beta_1 = \dfrac{[\ce{FeOH^{2+}}]}{[\ce{Fe^{3+}}][\ce{OH-}]} & \beta_2 = \dfrac{[\ce{Fe(OH)2+}]}{[\ce{Fe^{3+}}][\ce{OH-}]^2} & \beta_3 = \dfrac{[\ce{Fe(OH)3}]}{[\ce{Fe^{3+}}][\ce{OH-}]^3} \\ \hline \text{Constant value} & 10^{14} & 10^{25} & 10^{12} & 10^{22} & 10^{30} \end{array}$$

1. a) Calculate the fraction α of free $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$ cation in the solution at this pH.

b) Which process limits iron concentration in the solution at this pH?

c) Can one provide the required concentration of dissolved iron by adding, for example, iron(III) sulfate as fertilizer? Calculate the maximal total concertation of dissolved iron $c(\mathrm{Fe})$ in the aquarium.

2. Vasya was told that the plants consume iron more efficiently if its oxidation state is +2.

a) Which processes will start after the addition of iron(II) sulfate into this aquarium? Write the total reaction equation.

b) What percentage of dissolved iron will be present in the 2+ form, if $2\,\mathrm{\mu M}$ of iron(II) sulfate have been added at pH 7.2 and the equilibrium is reached?

3. There is a popular advice to increase the solubility of iron and its stability as iron(II) by adding iron as a chelate that can be prepared by mixing iron sulfate and EDTA.

a) Calculate the molar fraction of free $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$ $\alpha(\ce{Fe^{3+}})$ in the solution at this pH, if Vasya added simultaneously the iron salt ($2\,\mathrm{\mu M}$) and a 1.5-fold molar excess of EDTA. What is the dominating form of iron(III) under these conditions? Calculate its molar fraction.

b) Will iron(III) precipitate, if Vasya has added $2\,\mathrm{\mu M}$ of $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$ along with a 1.5-fold molar excess of EDTA? Confirm your answer by calculation.

c) Estimate which percent of dissolved iron is present as iron(II), if iron(II) is added simultaneously with a 1.5-molar excess of EDTA. Is it possible to preserve some noticeable amount of iron(II)?

problems.title: [Spectrophotometry of NAD+ and NADH]
problems.problem:
Problem 12 (Analytical Chemistry section, problem 3). [Spectrophotometry of NAD+ and NADH]

Spectrophotometry is sensitive method of analysis which allows determining small concentrations of compounds. This method is based on absorption of light of certain wavelength by molecules, which is related to specific electron transitions. The Beer-Lambert law describes the relation between light absorption and compound concentration: $A = \log\dfrac{I_0}{I} = \varepsilon cl = \sum_i \varepsilon_i c_i l$, where $A$ is absorbance, $I$ and $I_0$ are intensities of passed and initial light, $\varepsilon$ – extinction coefficient, $l$ – path length and $c$ – concentration. Absorption $A$ is additive quantity.

1. Choose all correct answers: absorbance: a) could be negative value, b) could be larger than 100, c) is always positive, d) does not depend on $\varepsilon$.

2. Express absorbance as function of light transmittance $\mathrm{T} = (I / I_0)\cdot100\%$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-12-fig1.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-12-fig2.png

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \lambda,\ \mathrm{nm} & A(2) & A(3) \\ \hline 260 & 0.981 & 1.047 \\ \hline 340 & 0.325 & 0.433 \end{array}$$

Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) is a coenzyme existing in oxidized ($\ce{NAD+}$) and reduced (NADH) forms (see the scheme) which take part in redox reactions of all live cells.

3. Write the reaction of oxalic acid $\ce{H2C2O4}$ oxidation by this coenzyme.

From initial solution $\mathbf{1}$ containing 25 mM of $\ce{NAD+}$ and a deficient quantity of $\ce{H2C2O4}$, a 5.0-mL aliquot was taken and diluted to 1000 mL, to obtain solution $\mathbf{2}$. The absorbance of solution $\mathbf{2}$ was measured at two wavelengths: 260 and 340 nm (A(2)). Simultaneously, 5.0 mL of 4.0 mM of NADH solution was diluted (to give solution $\mathbf{3}$) and absorbance A(3) was measured at the same both wavelengths. However, the laboratory assistant forgot what fold he diluted the solution. All the results are presented in the table. In all absorbance experiments $l = 5\,\mathrm{mm}$.

4. Using the absorption spectrum (see Fig.) point out which color has solution $\mathbf{1}$:

a) bluish, b) colorless, c) pale green, d) rich red.

5. At which wavelength in the range of 240 – 390 nm the light transmittance T of solution $\mathbf{1}$ is maximal?

6. From the table data, estimate the $\ce{NAD+}$ and NADH concentrations in solution $\mathbf{1}$ and find the extinction coefficients $\varepsilon$ for $\ce{NAD+}$ and NADH at 260 and 340 nm.

7. What fold did the poor laboratory assistant dilute the solution of NADH to obtain solution $\mathbf{3}$?

8. Estimate the minimal concentration of NAD detectable by this method (limit of detection), if the maximal detectable transmittance (T) is 99%.

problems.title: [Isomerization and aquatation of chromium(III) thiocyanate complexes]
problems.problem:
Problem 13 (Physical Chemistry section, problem 1). [Isomerization and aquatation of chromium(III) thiocyanate complexes]

For a great while isomerization of chromium thiocyanates has not been explored because of synthesis of one isomer failure.

1. Define isomerism type and write down structural formulae of fragments Cr–thiocyanate and Cr–isothiocyanate.

2. Point more stable isomer, if $\ce{Cr^{3+}}$ is a strong acid and thiocyanate ($\ce{SCN-}$) is weaker base than isothiocyanate ($\ce{NCS-}$).

In the mid-1960s Haim и Sutin succeeded to synthesize mixture of isothiocyanate (55 mol.%) and thiocyanate (45 mol.%) and to study kinetics of parallel running isomerization and aquatation. For the synthesis they used transfer of non-symmetrical bridge ligand and electron transfer in the reaction $\ce{[Co(en)2(H2O)NCS]^{2+} + [Cr(H2O)6]^{2+}}$.

3. Write down the reaction equation of synthesis $\ce{[Cr(H2O)5SCN]^{2+}}$ and draw the intermediate structure with non-symmetrical bridge –S–C–N–.

While studying kinetics they used bands in electronic spectrum $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ nm (initial solution, $\lambda_3$ is absent) and $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_3$ nm (final solution, $\lambda_2$ is absent), whereby $\lambda_2 > \lambda_3 > \lambda_1$.

4. Define complexes associated with these wave lengths if $\ce{NCS-}$ is ligand of strong, $\ce{H2O}$ – of middle and $\ce{SCN-}$ – weak field.

As a result of kinetic studies the relation for observed rate constant $k_\mathrm{obs} = f([\ce{H+}])$ was obtained and equation $k_\mathrm{obs} = (k_\mathrm{i} + k_\mathrm{a}) + [(k'_\mathrm{i} + k'_\mathrm{a})\cdot K_\mathrm{a}]/[\ce{H+}]$, where $k_\mathrm{i}$, $k'_\mathrm{i}$ – isomerization constants, $k_\mathrm{a}$ and $k'_\mathrm{a}$ – aquatation constants, was suggested.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} [\ce{H+}] & 4\cdot10^{-2} & 5\cdot10^{-2} & 8\cdot10^{-2} & 10\cdot10^{-2} \\ \hline k_\mathrm{obs},\ \mathrm{s^{-1}} & 4.27\cdot10^{-4} & 3.54\cdot10^{-4} & 2.44\cdot10^{-4} & 2.08\cdot10^{-4} \end{array}$$

5. Figure the plot $k_\mathrm{obs} = f(1/[\ce{H+}])$ and define how to obtain $(k_\mathrm{i} + k_\mathrm{a})$ and $(k'_\mathrm{i}\cdot K_\mathrm{a} + k'_\mathrm{a}\cdot K_\mathrm{a})$ from it. Calculate these values using $[\ce{H+}] = 5\cdot10^{-2}$ and $10\cdot10^{-2}$.

6. Calculate $k_\mathrm{i}$, $k_\mathrm{i}\cdot K_\mathrm{a}$, $k_\mathrm{a}$ and $k_\mathrm{a}\cdot K_\mathrm{a}$ if concentration ratio $\ce{[Cr(H2O)5NCS]^{2+}}$ to $\ce{[Cr(H2O)6]^{3+}}$ and $\ce{[Cr(H2O)4(OH)NCS]+}$ to $\ce{[Cr(H2O)4(OH)]^{2+}}$ in final system is 2.46 independently from $[\ce{H+}]$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-13-fig1.png

In opposition to isomerization, aquatation mechanism of this type of complexes has already been known ($k_\mathrm{obs} = k_\mathrm{u} + k_\mathrm{u}\cdot K_\mathrm{a}/[\ce{H+}]$).

7. Suggest similar to aquatation scheme of isomerization of $\ce{[Cr(H2O)5SCN]^{2+}}$ if the first reaction in both schemes is equal.

8. Derive the expression for isomerization $k_\mathrm{obs}$ ($[\ce{H+}] \gg K_\mathrm{a}$) by the stationary approximation method.

problems.title: [Redox flow batteries]
problems.problem:
Problem 14 (Physical Chemistry section, problem 2). [Redox flow batteries]

Redox flow battery is a promising type of chemical accumulators of electric energy. They are special in that the reactants yielding electricity in the redox reaction are stored in separate tanks in solutions and are pumped through an electrochemical cell where the redox reaction occurs. This provides virtually unlimited battery capacity as well as safety (since at any moment the reaction volume contains a small volume of solutions of the reacting species).

1. Draw the equations of half reactions occurring during charging of the flow battery containing solutions of iron(II) and iron(III) sulfates (electrolyte A) and chromium(II) and chromium(III) sulfates (electrolyte B) in aqueous sulfuric acid (pH = 0). Note: hereafter consider the standard conditions if not stated otherwise.

2. Calculate the voltage that can be achieved using the described battery.

3. State the side reaction that will compete with one of the reactions written in i. 1.

To avoid cross contamination of the anolyte and catholyte, it is preferable to use redox pairs containing the same metal in redox flow batteries. For example, compound $\mathbf{A}$ used in redox flow batteries contains 21.67 wt% M, 13.64 wt% S, and 61.26 wt% O.

4. Determine formula of $\mathbf{A}$ and metal M.

5. List the possible pairs of electrolytes (anolyte + catholyte) based on compounds of M suitable for redox flow batteries application. Confirm the answer by the necessary calculation, or draw the corresponding Frost diagram. (the solutions are considered different if different redox reactions occur during the battery operation when using the corresponding pairs)

6. Select the anolyte + catholyte pair providing the highest battery voltage.

Solutions of anolyte and catholyte are separated by semi-permeable membrane that is permeable to the ions providing for the solutions electroneutrality but prevents direct contact of the ions involved in the redox reaction (i. e. prevents anolyte and catholyte mixing).

7. Draw half reactions of oxidation and reduction of compounds corresponding to the compositions of anolyte and catholyte selected in i. 6. State the ions that should permeate through the membrane and these that should not pass through.

8. Calculate the volumes of the selected anolyte and catholyte required for substitution of the industrial UPS with net power 10 kW operating during 2 h from the internal battery. Assume that solubility of the anolyte and catholyte components equals 2 mol/L, 7% of the redox flow battery power is consumed to pump the solutions through the electrochemical cell, and redox reactions occur with 90% efficiency (if you have failed to select the electrolytes pair or calculate the electromotive force of the cell, use $E$ for the EMF and express the answer using this value).

Reference data: $E^\circ(\ce{Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}}) = 0.77\,\mathrm{V}$, $E^\circ(\ce{Cr^{3+}/Cr^{2+}}) = -0.41\,\mathrm{V}$, $E^\circ(\ce{H+/H2}) = 0.00\,\mathrm{V}$, $E^\circ(\ce{O2/H2O}) = 1.23\,\mathrm{V}$, $E^\circ(\mathrm{M^V/M^{IV}}) = 1.00\,\mathrm{V}$, $E^\circ(\mathrm{M^{IV}/M^{III}}) = 0.34\,\mathrm{V}$, $E^\circ(\mathrm{M^{III}/M^{II}}) = -0.25\,\mathrm{V}$, $E^\circ(\mathrm{M^{II}/M^0}) = -1.13\,\mathrm{V}$; $\Delta G^\circ = -nF(E^\circ_\mathrm{oxidant} - E^\circ_\mathrm{reductant})$

problems.title: [Equilibrium constants in strong electric and magnetic fields]
problems.problem:
Problem 15 (Physical Chemistry section, problem 3). [Equilibrium constants in strong electric and magnetic fields]

Strong electric and magnetic fields have influence on the equilibrium constant of a chemical reaction. Electrostatic field of high intensity exists near sharp ledges (tips) on the surface of charged conductors. A tip is characterized be the radius of rounding $r$ at its end, which can be brought to several hundreds of angstrom. If a tip is placed in the centre of a conducting sphere the construction shown in figure comes out. The volume of the sphere is filled with gaseous reaction mixture.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2017-2-15-fig1.png

Getting into the tip region, molecules are subjected to a strong electric field. On a small ball surface $E = q/4\pi\varepsilon\varepsilon_0 r^2$ (1).

1. Find the field intensity $E$ (V/m) on the surface of a tip, considering it to be a small ball with $r = 500\,\text{Å}$. Between the tip and the outer sphere electric tension $U = 2000\,\mathrm{V}$ is applied. Instructions: 1) Electric capacity of a ball $C = 4\pi\varepsilon\varepsilon_0 r$; 2) The relation between the ball charge and the tension $q = CU$.

In electric field there appears an additive member to the Gibbs energy of a compound, depending on intensity of the field: $G = G_0 - \tfrac{1}{2}PE$ (2), where $G_0$ – Gibbs energy without field, $P$ – complete dipole moment of matter. Due to this, in the expression of the reaction equilibrium constant $K = \exp(-\Delta_\mathrm{r}G^\circ/RT)$ additional factor appears:

$$K = K_0\exp\left\{\frac{E\left[\left(\sum\nu_iP_i\right)_\mathrm{product} - \left(\sum\nu_iP_i\right)_\mathrm{reagent}\right]}{2RT}\right\} = K_0\exp\left(\frac{E\cdot\Delta_\mathrm{r}P}{2RT}\right) \qquad (3)$$

$\nu_i$ – stoichiometrical coefficients in the reaction equation, $\Delta_\mathrm{r}P$ – dipole moment change in the reaction, $K_0$ – equilibrium constant without field.

2. In how many times will change the equilibrium constant of ideal-gas reaction

$$\ce{H2(g) + 1/2O2(g) = H2O(g)} \qquad (4)$$

at 300 K in the field 30 kV/cm, if to consider that the dipole moments of all molecules are directed along the field? Intrinsic dipole moment of $\ce{H2O}$ molecule $d_0 = 6.17\cdot10^{-30}\,\mathrm{C\cdot m}$. Instruction: Calculate $K/K_0 - 1$.

It is necessary to improve the calculation, because due to a thermal motion the dipole moments of gas molecules in the electric field are oriented according to Boltzmann distribution. Then the dipole moment of gas $P = V\chi E$ (5) depends on $E$ and temperature. Here $\chi(T)$ – dielectric receptivity of matter (dimensionless value in SGS system), $V$ – substance volume. Theory gives the following formula (in SGS system):

$$\chi = \frac{nd_0^2}{3k_\mathrm{B}T} \qquad (6)$$

where $n$ – number of molecules in a volume unit.

3. With the help of formula (2) deduce an expression (including only $d_0$, $E$ and $T$ as variables) for the Gibbs energy of 1 mol of gas in electric field at standard pressure $p^\circ = 101325\,\mathrm{Pa}$.

Influence of magnetic field on equilibrium constant of a reaction is described by an expression, analogous to (3). It is enough to do replacement $P \rightarrow M$, $E \rightarrow B$, where $B$ – magnetic induction, $M$ – complete magnetic moment of matter:

$$K = K_0\exp\left(\frac{B\cdot\Delta_\mathrm{r}M}{2RT}\right) \qquad (7)$$

Correlations, analogous to (5) и (6) also take place: $M = V\text{æ}B$ (8), $\text{æ} = n\mu_0^2/3k_\mathrm{B}T$ (9), where æ(T) – magnetic receptivity of matter (dimensionless value in SGS system), $\mu_0$ – intrinsic dipole moment of molecule.

4. Calculate, in how many times will change the equilibrium constant of reaction (4) in the field 30 kV/cm at 300 K. Instruction: Calculate $K/K_0 - 1$.

Molecule $\ce{O2}$ is one of the few diatomic molecules, having a different from zero spin in the ground state (triplet state), therefore oxygen is paramagnetic.

5. Specify the value of quantum number ($S$) for total spin of oxygen molecule and find the value of intrinsic magnetic moment of $\ce{O2}$ molecule in Bohr magnetons ($\mu_\mathrm{B}$) according to formula $\mu_0 = 2\mu_\mathrm{B}\sqrt{S(S+1)}$.

6. Calculate magnetic receptivity of gaseous oxygen at pressure $p^\circ$ and 300 K.

Magnetic resonance tomography (MRT), in which an organism is exposed to a strong magnetic field, is widely used in modern medicine. In high resolution devices magnetic induction may be as much as $B = 10000$ gausse (Gs). It is generally possible that the magnetic field influences on the chemical processes in a living being.

7. Verify this statement by calculating the change in equilibrium constant of reaction (4) at 300 K in a magnetic field with $B = 10000\,\mathrm{Gs}$? Instructions: 1) Use SGS units (cm, g, s, dyne, Gs); $1\,\mathrm{N} = 10^{5}\,\mathrm{dyne}$, $1\,\mathrm{J} = 10^{7}\,\mathrm{erg}$; 2) Calculate $K/K_0 - 1$.

Constants: $R = 8.314\,\mathrm{J/mol\cdot K}$, $k_\mathrm{B} = 1.38\cdot10^{-16}\,\mathrm{erg/K}$, $N_\mathrm{A} = 6.02\cdot10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$, $\mu_\mathrm{B} = 0.927\cdot10^{-20}\,\mathrm{erg/Gs}$.

problems.title: [An iron galvanic cell]
problems.problem:
Problem 1. [An iron galvanic cell]

«Each metal has a certain power, which is different from metal to metal, of setting the electricfluid in motion...» Alessandro Volta (1745–1827)

The first galvanic cell was invented in 1800 by A. Volta, which was based on the experiments of L. Galvani. Subsequently, galvanic elements have found wide application in science, technology and everyday life.

The left half-cell of the electrochemical element consists of an iron electrode (in excess) that is oxidized during the action and an aqueous solution of iron (III) nitrate with a concentration of 0.01 M. The right half-cell consists of graphite electrode and a mixture of iron (II) and (III) nitrates with concentrations of 0.05 M and 0.30 M, respectively. The volume of each half-cell is 1 L.

1. Indicate which of the electrodes is cathode and which is anode, and also indicate the kind of these two electrodes

2. Write schematically this cell as (–)… |…||…| …(+)

3. Write the half-reactions on each electrode and the total reaction

4. Using the information on ion mobility ($\mu^\circ$), select the most suitable ionic compound(s) for the salt bridge

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{Cation} & \mu^\circ,\ \mathrm{m^2\,V^{-1}\,s^{-1}}\cdot10^{9},\ 25\,^\circ\mathrm{C} & \text{Anion} & \mu^\circ,\ \mathrm{m^2\,V^{-1}\,s^{-1}}\cdot10^{9},\ 25\,^\circ\mathrm{C} \\ \hline \ce{Ca^{2+}}(\mathrm{aq}) & 61.6 & \ce{F^-}(\mathrm{aq}) & 51.5 \\ \hline \ce{K^+}(\mathrm{aq}) & 73.5 & \ce{CO3^{2-}}(\mathrm{aq}) & 70.3 \\ \hline \ce{NH4^+}(\mathrm{aq}) & 76.1 & \ce{NO3^-}(\mathrm{aq}) & 74.1 \\ \hline \ce{H^+}(\mathrm{aq}) & 205 & \ce{Br^-}(\mathrm{aq}) & 81.8 \end{array}$$

From the thermodynamic data it is known that the standard entropies of $\ce{Fe(s)}$, $\ce{Fe^{2+}(aq)}$ and $\ce{Fe^{3+}(aq)}$ at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ are 27.3, –137.7 and $-316.0\,\mathrm{J/mol\cdot K}$, respectively. An increase in temperature by $20\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ leads to a 85-fold decrease of total reaction equilibrium constant $K$.

5. a) Indicate an ion whose standard entropy in an aqueous solution is conditionally assumed to be zero b) Indicate the reason why the entropy of the triple-charged ion is much lower than that of the doubly charged ion (choose a case in the answer sheet); c) Calculate the entropy, enthalpy and Gibbs energy (at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) of full reaction. Consider that $\Delta_\mathrm{r}H^0$ and $\Delta_\mathrm{r}S^0$ are constant values in this temperature range. $R = 8.314\,\mathrm{J/mol\cdot K}$ and $F = 96485\,\mathrm{C/mol}$ (Faraday constant).

6. Calculate (in volts, accurate to 3 decimal places) the initial EMF of the cell and the initial potentials of the cathode and anode at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. It is known that $E^\circ(\ce{Fe^{2+}}/\ce{Fe}) = -0.447\,\mathrm{V}$.

The cell was working for 3 hours and 20 minutes until it was completely used.

7. What was the average current in the circuit?

problems.title: [Acid B from an elementary substance A]
problems.problem:
Problem 2. [Acid B from an elementary substance A]

Acid $\mathbf{B}$ (p$K_a$ = 0.77) can be conveniently prepared in the chemical laboratory by heating one of the acids $\mathbf{X}$ (p$K_a$ = –1.74), $\mathbf{Y}$ (p$K_a$ = –1) or $\mathbf{Z}$ (binary, p$K_a$ = 11.65) with an elementary substance $\mathbf{A}$, which exists as a solid at STP. Each of these reactions produces a gas, while the target compound, as very soluble substance, remains in the aqueous solution. After the reaction is complete, the aqueous solution is carefully evaporated to give the final product. When heating to $110\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the final product melts with decomposition to give substance $\mathbf{C}$ which contains 74.69% (by mass) of the chemical element of which $\mathbf{A}$ consists. Heating $\mathbf{C}$ in an air flow at $220\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ results in a loss of 1.77% of $\mathbf{C}$ by mass and produces solid $\mathbf{D}$. When $\mathbf{D}$ is heated in air to $300\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, it decomposes completely without a solid residue.

Calcination of an anhydrous barium salt of acid $\mathbf{B}$ in air results in a mass loss and produces salt $\mathbf{E}$, which cannot be obtained in aqueous solution.

When a 6.00 g of $\mathbf{B}$ is heated with excess of concentrated sulfuric acid, a certain compound $\mathbf{F}$ can be isolated from the reaction mixture. This reaction also produces $382\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ (STP) of a gas with a relative density of just above 1 with respect to air. Compound $\mathbf{F}$ contains 66.46% (by mass) of the chemical element comprising $\mathbf{A}$. When, after separation and drying, $\mathbf{F}$ is slowly rinsed with cold water on a glass filter, it turns into substance $\mathbf{G}$ which has the same qualitative composition as $\mathbf{D}$ but with 1.190 times less oxygen (by mass).

1. Determine the chemical formulas of $\mathbf{A}$ – $\mathbf{D}$, $\mathbf{X}$, $\mathbf{Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$.

2. Write down the chemical equations representing the three methods of preparation of acid $\mathbf{B}$.

3. Identify salt $\mathbf{E}$ and write down the chemical equation representing its preparation.

4. Identify compound $\mathbf{F}$ and write down the equation representing its preparation.

5. Identify substance $\mathbf{G}$ and write down the equations for the corresponding reactions.

6. In an aqueous solution under ambient conditions, acid $\mathbf{B}$ reacts with acid $\mathbf{H}$ to form two new acids. Write a chemical equation of this reaction.

problems.title: [An aramid fibre from recycled PET]
problems.problem:
Problem 3. [An aramid fibre from recycled PET]

In mid-1960ies, a high-strength fiber based on polymer $\mathbf{X}$ (prepared via polycondensation of equimolar mixture of monomers $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{F}$) was developed at DuPont laboratories. Owing to the formation of intermolecular hydrogen bonds, the fiber is resistant to dynamic stresses (several times stronger than steel). The fiber is currently used for manufacturing of light-weight durable parts of sport equipment, body armors, ropes, and cables. The fiber retains its excellent mechanical properties at temperatures within the range of −196 to $420\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, allowing its applications in the development of fire-fighting and cryogenic equipment.

$\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{F}$ can be obtained via recycling of plastic bottles made of polyethylene terephthalate (PET).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-1-3-fig1.png

1. Identify the transformations involved in PET recycling.

2. a) Draw the structure of the repeating unit of $\mathbf{X}$.

b) Determine the average polymerization degree $n$ (number of the repeating units) in the polymer prepared from $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{F}$ under equilibrium conditions; the equilibrium constant of interaction between functional groups of $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{F}$ $K_\mathrm{eq} = 10^6$.

3. How many bottles (20 g each) should be subjected to recycling to manufacture a body armor containing 2 kg of $\mathbf{X}$, if each of the stages on the above scheme proceeds with a 90% yield (consider the PET → $\mathbf{A}$ transformation as a single stage)?

4. Depict the hydrogen bonds formed between polymer chains (draw at least two repeating units in each chain). Give the number of hydrogen bonds per one repeating unit.

$\mathbf{X}$ is stable when in contact with neutral and alkaline media, but is hydrolyzed in acidic medium.

5. Calculate the masses of 60·60 cm protective elements of body armors made of steel and of the fiber $\mathbf{X}$, both capable of stopping a 4.7 g bullet with 5 mm diameter moving at the velocity of $247\,\mathrm{m/s}$ perpendicular to the armor. $\rho_\mathrm{steel} = 7.7\,\mathrm{g/cm^3}$, $\rho_\mathbf{X} = 1.44\,\mathrm{g/cm^3}$. Depth of a bullet penetration is given by the formula: $L = \alpha\cdot m\cdot\left(\dfrac{V}{d}\right)^2$, where $d$, $V$, and $m$ are the bullet diameter, velocity, and mass, respectively. The values of parameter α for steel and $\mathbf{X}$ are $5.84\cdot10^{-10}$ and $1.35\cdot10^{-9}\,\mathrm{m\cdot s^2/kg}$, respectively.

problems.title: [The chemistry of matches]
problems.problem:
Problem 4. [The chemistry of matches]

Until the middle of the XIX century, kindling the fire was very tedious. Radical changes occurred with the discovery of substances that can ignite at fairly low temperatures. The first step to creating the prototypes of modern matches was made in 1805. The head of the first matches was covered with a mixture of substances $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{C}$, powdered sugar and resin extracted from the acacia. However, they were ignited not from friction, but when the match was immersed in concentrated $\ce{H2SO4}$. The matches made in 1826 become more convenient in use. The heads of these matches consisted of substances $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{D}$ and also acacia resin. The disadvantage of this option was the allocation of a large amount of gas $\mathbf{E}$ with an unpleasant odor. In order to eliminate this disadvantage, in 1830 matches were proposed that ignited with reaction $\mathbf{A}$ and poisonous substance $\mathbf{F}$, which was initiated even by the slightest friction. To reduce the risk of autoignition, in 1836 substance $\mathbf{A}$ was replaced by $\mathbf{G}$. To create "safe matches" $\mathbf{F}$ was replaced by a non-toxic substance $\mathbf{J}$, formed by slow heating of $\mathbf{F}$ in a sealed vessel. By the beginning of the XX century, matches were being made, based on substances $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{H}$, which was obtained by heating $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ above $100\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

1. Determine the substances $\mathbf{A}$ – $\mathbf{J}$, $\mathbf{L}$. If it is known that:

1) gas $\mathbf{E}$ is formed by burning in a oxygen of $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{D}$, $\mathbf{H}$ and $\mathbf{L}$.

2) the mass fraction of $\mathbf{B}$ in the substance $\mathbf{H}$ is 43.6%.

3) at a reaction between $\mathbf{G}$ and 0.80 g of $\mathbf{B}$ 690 mL of gas $\mathbf{E}$ ($400\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, 1 atm) are released and 2.99 g of a black solid $\mathbf{L}$ are formed ($\mathbf{G} + 2\mathbf{B} \rightarrow \mathbf{E} + \mathbf{L}$) which oxidizes in an oxygen flow at $1200\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and 1 atm pressure, also with an $\mathbf{E}$ release of 1.51 L ($2\mathbf{L} + 3\ce{O2} \rightarrow 2\mathbf{E} + \ldots$).

4) $\mathbf{C}$ is reduced by iron to the metal which exists in the liquid aggregate state at the normal condition.

5) the unit cell of $\mathbf{D}$ has the following parameters: $a = 1.131$, $b = 0.3837$, $c = 1.123\,\mathrm{nm}$, $\alpha = \beta = \gamma = 90^\circ$, number of formula units $z = 4$. The calculated density of $\mathbf{D}$ is $4.63\,\mathrm{g/cm^3}$.

6) substance $\mathbf{A}$ was first obtained in just 19 years before its application in the production of matches when passing chlorine through a hot KOH solution.

7) $\mathbf{F}$ has a high reactivity, burns in $\ce{Br2}$ and $\ce{Cl2}$, is easily oxidized by air oxygen. Directly does not interact with hydrogen, but hydride of $\mathbf{F}$ can be obtained by its interaction with a solution of alkali.

2. Write the reaction equations:

a) $\mathbf{A} + \ce{C12H22O11} \xrightarrow{\ce{H2SO4}}$

b) $\mathbf{A} + \mathbf{D} \xrightarrow{\text{friction}}$

c) $\mathbf{A} + \mathbf{J} \xrightarrow{\text{friction}}$

d) $\mathbf{G} + \mathbf{J} \xrightarrow{\text{friction}}$

e) $\mathbf{A} + \mathbf{H} \xrightarrow{\text{friction}}$

problems.title: [Oxidation of a vegetable fat]
problems.problem:
Problem 5. [Oxidation of a vegetable fat]

On prolonged frying or storage, fats accumulate radical oxidation products. Oxidation of fats is studied by heating them in the presence of oxygen. One and the same vegetable fat was subjected to various treatments.

1. A weight of initial triglyceride (88 mg) was dissolved in a suitable solvent, acetic acid and 0.5 mL of a 5.0 M hydrogen peroxide solution were added (in this case, peracetic acid was formed, that transfers the $\ce{C=C}$ bond to the epoxide). The excess of peroxide remaining after the reaction liberated iodine from KI. The amount of iodine was equivalent to 8.8 mL of 0.50 M solution of thiosulfate. Considering epoxidation quantitative, estimate the number of double bonds in the sample. Write down the necessary reaction equations and the structure of the original fat, if all the fatty acid residues in it are the same.

2. Another portion of the same fat weighed 10 g was heated for a long time in air at $50\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. As a result, hydroperoxides containing C–O–O–H fragment were formed. An excess of KI was added to the fat and the liberated iodine was titrated with 2.2 mL of 0.100 M thiosulphate. Draw the structure of one of the monohydroperoxides (if only one of the fatty acid residues reacts) and write down the reactions of its formation and interaction with KI in an acidic medium. Calculate the peroxide number of fat PN (mmol of absorbed $\ce{O2}$ / kg fat).

3. a) The same fat in the amount of 88 mg (if you did not determine the structure of fat in paragraph 1, take its molar mass equal to 700 g/mol) was emulsified in a surfactant solution and oxidized with permanganate in an acidic medium with heating, which required 0.48 mmol of $\ce{KMnO4}$. How many electrons does a fat molecule lose in this reaction? Write down the formulas of the products formed upon the oxidation of fat with $\ce{KMnO4}$.

b) A similar procedure conducted with 88 mg of fat containing hydroperoxides required 0.54 mmol of $\ce{KMnO4}$. Write down the reaction equation of the thermal degradation product with permanganate if the peroxy group is transformed into keto group. Calculate the number of hydroperoxide groups per fat molecule.

problems.title: [McMurry's in/out-bicycloalkanes]
problems.problem:
Problem 6. [McMurry's in/out-bicycloalkanes]

In 1984, the research group led by John McMurry (an American chemist, the author of the well-known textbook "Organic Chemistry", which has already undergone the 9th edition) synthesized interesting bridged polycyclic compounds $\mathbf{I}$ and $\mathbf{II}$ according to the scheme:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-1-6-fig1.png

1. In the synthesis of $\mathbf{I}$, the conversion of $\mathbf{D}$ into $\mathbf{II}$ is so-called McMurry reaction. If $\ce{C3H6O}$ ($\mathbf{III}$) is used in this reaction (instead of $\mathbf{D}$), then a compound $\ce{C6H12}$ ($\mathbf{IV}$) will be obtained. Determine the structures of $\mathbf{III}$ and $\mathbf{IV}$ if IR spectrum of $\mathbf{III}$ exhibits an intense absorption band at $1715\,\mathrm{cm^{-1}}$, and only one singlet is detected in the $^1$H NMR spectrum of $\mathbf{IV}$.

Compounds $\mathbf{I}$ and $\mathbf{II}$ are characterized by an unusual type of stereoisomerism – the so-called in/out-isomerism.

2. Draw the structural formulas of $\mathbf{Ia}$ and $\mathbf{Ib}$ (in,in- and out,out-stereoisomers of $\mathbf{I}$, respectively).

3. Determine the structures of $\mathbf{A}$ – $\mathbf{D}$, RMgCl, $\mathbf{II}$ and suggest the reagents for the stage $\mathbf{II} \rightarrow \mathbf{I}$ if the $^1$H NMR spectrum of the Grignard reagent RMgCl ($w_\mathrm{C} = 59.24\%$, $w_\mathrm{Mg} = 10.90\%$) includes a singlet, triplet, triplet, quintet, quintet and multiplet ($\delta = 7.5$ ppm) with an integral intensity ratio of 2:2:2:2:2:5, and $\mathbf{B}$ contains an endocyclic double bond. Specify the $\mathbf{B}$ configuration ($Z$/$E$).

When $\mathbf{II}$ is treated with $\ce{CF3COOH}$ at $40\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, it is quantitatively converted to [$\mathbf{V}$], which has an increased stability for this class of intermediates. Alternatively, [$\mathbf{V}$] can be synthesized from $\mathbf{I}$ by the action of trifluoromethanesulfonic acid, which is accompanied by the release of gas $\mathbf{X}$. The structure of [$\mathbf{V}$] contains a bridged two-electron three-center bond and is more symmetric in comparison with $\mathbf{I}$, as evidenced by the $^1$H NMR spectrum (in particular, the molecule of [$\mathbf{V}$] has one more symmetry plane than $\mathbf{I}$). The described regularities and increased stability of [$\mathbf{V}$] are due to the fact that two resonance structures can be represented for it:

$$[\mathbf{V}] = [\mathbf{Va} \longleftrightarrow \mathbf{Vb}]$$

4. Write the structural formulas of [$\mathbf{V}$], $\mathbf{Va}$, $\mathbf{Vb}$, $\mathbf{X}$. Suppose which of the in/out-stereoisomers of $\mathbf{I}$ ($\mathbf{Ia}$ or $\mathbf{Ib}$) can exhibit similar reactivity.

problems.title: [Kinetics of a consecutive reaction by UV-vis spectroscopy]
problems.problem:
Problem 7. [Kinetics of a consecutive reaction by UV-vis spectroscopy]

Some irreversible chemical conversion of a substance $\mathbf{X}$ to a substance $\mathbf{W}$ that takes place in a solution and includes only successive steps was studied by means of UV-vis spectroscopy at the wavelength $\lambda_1 = 320\,\mathrm{nm}$ in a cuvette with optical path length 0.5 cm. Before all, solution 0.00131 M of pure substance $\mathbf{X}$ was taken. Obtained dependence of absorbance ($A$) on time is in the table below.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c} t,\ \mathrm{min} & 0 & 2 & 4 & 6 & 10 & 20 & 50 & 100 & \infty \\ \hline A & 0.982 & 2.073 & 2.538 & 2.727 & 2.883 & 2.713 & 2.369 & 1.919 & 0.681 \end{array}$$

1. What is minimum number of the successive stages in the conversion of $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{W}$?

2. Calculate molar extinction coefficient (indicate its dimension) of substance $\mathbf{X}$ at the mentioned wavelength.

3. A series of standard solutions of final product ($\mathbf{W}$) was investigated by means of UV-vis spectroscopy at 320 nm in a cuvette with optical path length 1 cm. Calculate the molar extinction coefficient for $\mathbf{W}$ using the data below.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} c(\mathbf{W}),\ \mathrm{M} & 0.00100 & 0.00200 & 0.00300 & 0.00500 \\ \hline \mathrm{A} & 0.56 & 1.08 & 1.60 & 2.64 \end{array}$$

4. Accept the number of stages that you suggested (1st order) and write down a scheme of the conversion of $\mathbf{X}$ (use the results of point 3).

5. Estimate molar extinction coefficient at 320 nm for every intermediate in the scheme you proposed.

6. Estimate every rate constant in the scheme you proposed.

7. Initial and final substances have an isosbestic point at the wavelength $\lambda_2 = 710\,\mathrm{nm}$, and none of the intermediate substances absorbs light. Schematically depict the dependence of the optical density on time if the solution is monitored at this wavelength (include point $t = \infty$). Indicate characteristic properties of the dependence if any.

Additional information: Beer – Lambert – Bouguer law: $A = \varepsilon lc$, for a 1st order reaction: $c(t) = c_0\cdot\exp(-kt)$. Isosbestic point of a couple of substances is the wavelength where molar extinction coefficients of both substances are equal.

problems.title: Synthons for Vermiculin
problems.problem:
Problem 8. Synthons for Vermiculin

The term “synthon” was coined in 1967 by E.J. Corey. Its term means a real or idealized structural unit of a molecule that can be introduced into chemical synthesis by known techniques. Synthon does not exist as a specific reagent; it is a formal particle (ion, radical or carbene). Each synthon can be associated with one or more real reagents, and conversely, one reagent could be a synthetic equivalent for a few synthons. The prominent example of such dual reagents in formaldehyde, which can act as a C$_1$-electrophile, but upon transformation into 1,3-dithiane $\mathbf{I}$ undergoes a retrosynthetic umpolung to C$_1$-nucleophile. The real nucleophilic reagent in the case is organolithium compound $\mathbf{II}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-1-8-fig1.png

1. Decipher the substances $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{D}$, $\mathbf{F}$, $\mathbf{G}$, $\mathbf{II}$.

Compound $\mathbf{II}$ is successfully applied for the selective synthesis of homo- and polyfunctional compounds (see scheme at right)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-1-8-fig2.png

2. Decipher the substances $\mathbf{H}$, $\mathbf{X}$, $\mathbf{J}$, $\mathbf{K}$, $\mathbf{L}$, if $\mathbf{J}$, $\mathbf{L}$ and $\mathbf{C}$ are isomers, which NMR $^1$H spectra possess signals at ~ 10 ppm: doublet (for $\mathbf{L}$ and $\mathbf{C}$) or triplet (for $\mathbf{J}$).

The using of dithiane $\mathbf{I}$ leads to development of effective "short" synthesis of polyfunctional natural compounds, for example, an antibiotic, vermiculin ($\mathbf{IV}$), isolated from Talaromyces vermiculatus:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-1-8-fig3.png

3. Decipher the substances $\mathbf{M}$, $\mathbf{N}$, $\mathbf{O}$, $\mathbf{P}$, $\mathbf{Q}$, $\mathbf{R}$, $\mathbf{S}$, $\mathbf{T}$ from Scheme, if known that MW ($\mathbf{IV}$) less than the molar mass of Q by 8.64%. Structures $\mathbf{T}$ and $\mathbf{III}$ – isocyclic; the molecule $\mathbf{T}$ have the number of hydrogen atoms is twice as large, and the oxygen atoms are half as much as in comparison with $\mathbf{VI}$, and the number of carbon atoms in $\mathbf{T}$ is 60% larger than in $\mathbf{VI}$.

problems.title: [Harmful amino acids and adducts formed in cooking]
problems.problem:
Problem 1 (Life Sciences and Polymers section, problem 1). [Harmful amino acids and adducts formed in cooking]

Both industrial and home cooking can lead to substances potentially harmful to man. The reasons include high temperatures, extreme pH and non-natural compounds (e.g. preservation agents).

A non-canonical α-amino acid $\mathbf{A}$ (40.44% C, 7.92% H, 15.72% N, and 35.92% O by mass) is formed from a canonical amino acid $\mathbf{B}$, for example as a result of soya bean processing into its hydrolysate.

1. Draw the structures of the amino acids $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ with stereochemical details, if no other initial compounds but $\mathbf{B}$ are needed in the reaction of $\mathbf{A}$ formation.

$\mathbf{A}$ is one of substrates in the enzymatic synthesis of a dipeptide $\mathbf{C}$ (26.1% C, 52.2 % H, and 13.0% O by moles) occurring in bacteria. $\mathbf{C}$ is found in the cell wall peptidoglycan as a terminal residue, and is vitally important for the bacteria stability. Alkaline hydrolysis of $\mathbf{C}$ under extreme conditions leads to the formation of an optically inactive substance $\mathbf{D}$ as the only product.

2. Deduce $\mathbf{C}$ and $\mathbf{D}$.

The amino acid $\mathbf{X}$ causes high nephrotoxicity in mice. The $\mathbf{X}$ residue can be formed upon heat treatment of protein containing food in alkaline medium (e.g., upon milk sterilization). The $\mathbf{X}$ residue is formed due to a modification of the side chain of the canonical amino acid $L$-lysine.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-2-1-fig1.png

It is worth mentioning that there is a stable intermediate interacting non-enzymatically with the lysine residue at the stage of $\mathbf{X}$ formation. The intermediate is the residue of a non-canonical α-amino acid $\mathbf{Y}$ (41.38% C, 5.79% H, 16.09% N, and 36.74% O by mass), which cannot be isolated in a free form because of its low stability.

3. Draw the structures of $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ with stereochemical details.

4. Write down the reaction equations explaining extreme instability of $\mathbf{Y}$ in an aqueous solution.

5. Propose the structural formulae of two canonical amino acids (without stereochemical details), residues of which in a protein can form the $\mathbf{Y}$ residue in one stage at pH≥10.

Acrylamide is another toxic substance formed during cooking. It is transformed into glycidamide in a process catalyzed by the cytochrome P450 dependent monooxygenase. Glycidamide interacts with DNA nitrogenous bases (a nitrogen atom in the cycle is being attacked), which is behind mutagenic action of the substance.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-2-1-fig2.png

It was demonstrated that $\mathbf{Z}$ reacts with 2'-deoxycytidine in a buffer solution with the formation of two products $\mathbf{Z1}$ (45.71% C, 35.53% O, and 13.33% N by mass) and $\mathbf{Z2}$ (45.57% C, 40.47% O, and 8.86% N by mass).

6. Draw the structural formulae of $\mathbf{Z1}$ and $\mathbf{Z2}$, if it is known that $\mathbf{Z2}$ (by contrast to $\mathbf{Z1}$) is a 2'-deoxyuridine derivative.

The structures of nitrogenous bases are:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-2-1-fig3.png

problems.problem:
Problem 2 (Life Sciences and Polymers section, problem 2). [Glucose: dehydration, caramelization and carbonaceous nanoparticles]

Reactions of carbohydrates are important in living things. However, even in the absence of additional reactants, various reactions can occur in aqueous solutions of sugars.

1. Based on the Fischer projection of D-glucose given in the Answers Sheet, draw all its cyclic forms coexisting in its aqueous solution.

Microwave treatment of a glucose solution in aqueous sulfuric acid leads to the formation of valuable products. One of these, $\mathbf{A}$ ($^1$H NMR, ppm: 9.59 s, 1H; 7.22 d, 1H; 6.52 d, 1H; 4.73 s, 2H; 3.73 broad s, ex. with $\ce{D2O}$) is a product of elimination of three water molecules from glucose. It is the formation of $\mathbf{A}$ in acidic medium that determines the sample coloration in the Molisch’s test for carbohydrates (the reaction with phenols). Reduction of $\mathbf{A}$ affords $\mathbf{B}$ which is used in the synthesis of polyurethanes. The $^1$H NMR spectra of $\mathbf{B}$ posess 3 signals, one of these exchange with $\ce{D2O}$.

2. Draw the structures of $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, copolymer of $\mathbf{B}$ with hexamethylene-1,6-diisocyanate, and the product of interaction of $\mathbf{A}$ with two molecules of α-naphthol.

Heating of an aqueous solution of carbohydrates leads to its transformation into dark viscous mass (this is the way to caramel). The selectivity of the process being poor due to high temperature, the product mixture contains hundreds of compounds formed via isomerization, dehydration, condensation, and disproportionation. The overall process can be illustrated by the van Krevelen diagram (with the H/C and O/C ratios in the products at the axes, each product being represented by a point).

3. a) At the van Krevelen diagram of the products of glucose caramelization (see the Answers Sheet), draw an arrow showing the exact direction corresponding to the intramolecular dehydration. Calculate the slope of the arrow referred to the horizontal axis.

b) From the list given there, choose the type of reactions leading to the group III products.

Caramelization of glucose occurs at $160\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, therefore heating of the aqueous solution leads first to evaporation of the major fraction of water, and the reactions take place practically in the glucose melt. Heating in a sealed vessel (autoclaving) allows attaining high temperature even of dilute solutions. Autoclaving brings water to the subcritical state with significantly decreased dielectric constant, making possible reactions atypical for aqueous solutions. Autoclaving of aqueous solutions of glucose affords nanoparticles with the graphite core and the surface bearing different oxygen-containing functional groups.

4. A small fraction of similar products is formed during caramelization at atmospheric pressure. Which group number at the van Krevelen diagram such products belong to?

Composition of the autoclaving products is described by the content of the functional groups per substance mass rather than by conventional formulas. The Boehm titration described below is a convenient method of analysis of carbonaceous particles. Two portions of the particles (0.5000 g each) were incubated in aqueous solutions of sodium hydrocarbonate and sodium hydroxide (concentration of each 0.1000 M, volume of each 50.00 mL). The precipitates were then discarded, and 10.00 mL aliquots of 1.000 M hydrochloric acid were added to each filtrate. The filtrates were boiled and titrated with 1.000 M of sodium hydroxide solution. 7.10 and 8.35 mL of the titrant were consumed, respectively.

5. Suppose that only carboxylic and phenolic oxygen-containing groups are found at the particles surface. Determine the quantities of these groups per 1.000 g of the particles.

Since acidic groups are found at the surface of the prepared particles, the latter can be used for removal of basic pollutants (e.g. bactericide agent Biopag) from an aqueous solution.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-2-2-fig1.png

The interaction of equal volumes (1 L each) of aqueous solutions (both at pH 4) of Biopag (44.43 g/L) and polyacrylic acid (18.00 g/L) resulted in the release of additional 0.22 mol of protons into the solution. The insoluble product did not contain chloride ions, and polyacrylic acid was not found in the solution.

6. Calculate the fraction of Biopag left over in the solution after the interaction with polyacrylic acid and the mass fraction of Biopag in the dried precipitate.

7. Calculate the maximum mass of Biopag which can be removed from its aqueous solution using 1.000 g of nanoparticles described in i. 5. Suppose equal efficiency of Biopag interaction with the acidic groups of polyacrylic acid and the carbonaceous nanoparticles.

In 2017, the HVMN Company commercialized Ketone, a novel energy drink based on the compound $\mathbf{X}$ and designed to improve the athletes’ results.

problems.title: Organometallic reagents
problems.problem:
Problem 4 (Organic Chemistry section, problem 1). Organometallic reagents

Organometallic compounds $\mathbf{I}$–$\mathbf{V}$ based on the element $\mathbf{X}$ are important reagents in organic chemistry. Most of them are derivatives of $\mathbf{X}$, containing cyclopentadienyl (Cp or $\ce{C5H5}$) ligand, which can be obtained from binary compound $\mathbf{A}$. Thus, by treating the liquid chloride $\mathbf{A}$, which intensively emits fumes when exposed to air, with sodium cyclopentadienide in tetrahydrofuran (THF), the bright red crystals of compound $\mathbf{I}$ ($w(\mathbf{X}) = 19.23\%$) are formed. $\mathbf{I}$ is the starting compound for other cyclopentadienyl complexes of $\mathbf{X}$ synthesis. When $\mathbf{I}$ is reduced with magnesium in the atmosphere of CO, the maroon complex $\mathbf{II}$ ($w(\mathbf{X}) = 20.45\%$) is formed. But if $\mathbf{I}$ is reduced with zinc in tetrahydrofuran, the green crystals of compound $\mathbf{III}$ ($w(\mathbf{X}) = 22.42\%$) can be extracted, which exists in free form as a dimer. The treatment of $\mathbf{I}$ with the excess of MeLi leads to the formation of $\mathbf{IV}$ ($w(\mathbf{X}) = 23.00\%$), and if $\mathbf{I}$ is reacted with 2 equivalents of $\ce{Me3Al}$ in toluene, the binuclear complex $\mathbf{V}$ ($w(\mathbf{X}) = 16.82\%$) is formed, which has 2 tetrahedral metallic centers connected to each other with two bridging ligands. In this reaction the compound $\mathbf{Y}$ ($w(\mathrm{Al}) = 29.17\%$) is also formed and methane releases. The compounds $\mathbf{IV}$ and $\mathbf{V}$ are precursors of highly reactive molecule $\mathbf{Z}$, what is more, it can be generated from $\mathbf{IV}$ by heating or from $\mathbf{V}$ by pyridine treatment.

1. Determine the element $\mathbf{X}$ and compound $\mathbf{A}$. Draw structural formulae of complex compounds $\mathbf{I}$–$\mathbf{V}$, molecule $\mathbf{Z}$ and compound $\mathbf{Y}$. In complexes $\mathbf{I}$–$\mathbf{V}$ and compounds $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ indicate the formal oxidation state of element $\mathbf{X}$.

The diversity of mentioned reagents possibilities can be illustrated with the following schemes:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-2-4-fig1.png

2. Draw the structural formulae of compounds $\mathbf{B}$ – $\mathbf{F}$, if it is known, that compound $\mathbf{B}$ is thermodynamically more stable isomer, and $\mathbf{C}$ is chiral. Correlate the reagents $\mathbf{II}$ – $\mathbf{V}$ with their role in organic transformations (olefinating reagent, deoxygenative reagent, one-electron reductant).

problems.title: [Sumanene]
problems.problem:
Problem 5 (Organic Chemistry section, problem 2). [Sumanene]

Sumanene (from Hindi "flower") is a conjugated hydrocarbon $\mathbf{X}$ ($\ce{C21H12}$), which can be considered as a fullerene fragment. Attempts to synthesize $\mathbf{X}$ began in 1993 with the pyrolysis of the corresponding substance $\mathbf{A}$. However, during this sythesis, only compounds $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{C}$ were isolated with a low yield.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-2-5-fig1.png

1. Give the structures of sumanene $\mathbf{X}$ and compounds $\mathbf{A}$ – $\mathbf{C}$

Successful synthesis of Sumanene $\mathbf{X}$ was realized only 10 years later, in 2003. The synthesis began from hydrocarbon $\mathbf{F}$, which has 3 signals in the $^1$H NMR spectrum (int 2:1:1) and 3 signals in the $^{13}$C NMR spectrum. In his turn, hydrocarbon $\mathbf{F}$ is obtained by the reaction of equimolar addition of hydrocarbon $\mathbf{D}$ and gas $\mathbf{E}$ ($w_\mathrm{C} = 92.3\%$). A further step was the modification of $\mathbf{F}$ to form a bifunctional compound $\mathbf{G}$, which, under the action of copper (I) salts, gives a mixture of hydrocarbons $\mathbf{H1}$ and $\mathbf{H2}$ in a ratio of 1:3 with the brute formula $\ce{C21H18}$. The major $\mathbf{H2}$ isomer under olefin metathesis conditions leads to hydrocarbon $\mathbf{J}$. At the same time, the minor isomer of $\mathbf{H1}$ under similar conditions leads to compound $\mathbf{I}$, which during oxidation gave the desired sumanene $\mathbf{X}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-2-5-fig2.png

2. Give the structural formulae of compounds $\mathbf{D}$ – $\mathbf{J}$.

The sumanene which was synthetized, possesses a number of interesting properties. Thus, there are two doublets in the $^1$H NMR spectrum of sumanene at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ at 3.42 and 4.71 ppm, which, when heated to $140\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, merge into a wide signal. For a more detailed study of this phenomenon, a deuterated derivative of $\mathbf{Y}$ was obtained according to the scheme given below. Compound $\mathbf{Y}$ at room temperature in the NMR spectrum gave two singlets at 3.42 and 4.71 ppm. with equal intensities, which indicated the existence of $\mathbf{Y}$ in two forms. In addition, it was found that the transition frequency between these two forms was $0.066\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and $0.007\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ at 318 K and 298 K, respectively.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/imcho-2018-2-5-fig3.png

3. Draw the structural formulae of $\mathbf{Y}$ and anion $\mathbf{Z}$.

4. Show the structures of two forms of $\mathbf{Y}$, which has the corresponding signals in NMR: 3.42 and 4.71 ppm

5. Calculate the activation energy to pass from one form of $\mathbf{Y}$ to another.

In 1992, substance $\mathbf{X}$ later called halomon, was isolated from the red alga Portieria hornemannii. Problem 7 (Analytical Chemistry section, problem 1). [Water softening with EDTA]

Salts of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA, $\ce{H4Y}$) form very stable $\mathrm{MetY}^{(4-x)-}$ complexes with many $\mathrm{Met}^{x+}$ metal ions. EDTA is used in textile, paper, paint, and other industries to soften industrial water, as well as in analytical chemistry. EDTA is a weak acid, its dissociation constants are as follows: $K_1 = 1.0\cdot10^{-2}$; $K_2 = 2.1\cdot10^{-3}$; $K_3 = 6.9\cdot10^{-7}$; $K_4 = 5.5\cdot10^{-11}$.

c. The maximum possible pH of the water described in the problem situation is determined by the precipitation of insoluble carbonates. Calculate this value, assuming the system is in equilibrium. Solubility products: $K_\mathrm{S}(\ce{CaCO3}) = 3.8\cdot10^{-9}$, $K_\mathrm{S}(\ce{MgCO3}) = 2.1\cdot10^{-5}$.
